definition_zh: 房东；地主；（旧）旅店老板；客栈掌柜
definition_en: the person who owns a house or room and lets it to tenants, also a dated word for an innkeeper or the owner of land
core_image: 一个人站在自家楼门口，手里捏着一串钥匙和一沓房租收据
scene: 冬天的清晨，楼道里的暖气还没热起来。The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 landlord 指「房东」（第 1 个义项）；句意为房东敲门来收房租。图中可辨识物件：楼门、钥匙串、房租收据。

derivatives.zh: 由 land 与 lady 复合，指女房东、女店主
由 landlord 加 -ism 构成，指地主收租的制度
由 landlord 加 -ing 构成，指出租房屋收租的行当

senses.title: The owner of property that is rented out
senses.definition: the person who owns a house, flat or room and lets it to someone who pays rent
senses.definitionCN: 拥有房屋、公寓或房间并出租给交租金者的人
senses.example: The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东敲门来收房租。
senses.why: Once houses were let for money, the man who held the land also held the keys, so the compound shifted from owning ground to receiving rent.
senses.whyCN: 当房屋开始出租换钱，握有土地的人也握有钥匙，于是这个复合词从「拥有土地」转向「收取租金」。

senses.title: The keeper of an inn or a pub
senses.definition: a dated word for the man who runs an inn, a boarding house or a pub
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法，指经营旅店、寄宿舍或酒馆的男子
senses.example: The landlord of the old inn kept a fire burning all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老旅店的老板整个冬天都让炉火不灭。
senses.why: An innkeeper owned the building he worked in, so the word for a property owner naturally covered the man behind the bar.
senses.whyCN: 旅店老板拥有自己经营的房子，因此「房产所有者」这个词自然也能指吧台后面的那个人。

senses.title: The lord of a manor
senses.definition: a historical word for the man who held land from a superior and ruled the tenants on it
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，指从上级领有土地并管束其佃户的男子
senses.example: The landlord of the manor also judged disputes among his tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园领主还裁决佃户之间的纠纷。
senses.why: In the feudal order land carried power, so landlord named not just an owner but the man whose word settled what happened on his ground.
senses.whyCN: 在封建秩序里土地意味着权力，因此 landlord 不只指所有者，还指那个一句话就能决定自己地界上事务的人。

intro.en: Landlord is a Middle English compound of land and lord, and lord itself goes back to an Old English word for the keeper of the loaf.
intro.cn: landlord 是中古英语由 land 与 lord 构成的复合词，而 lord 又可追到古英语中「掌管面包者」一词。

items.en: Land meant ground, territory or a country, and it is one of the oldest Germanic words in English.
items.cn: land 指土地、领土或国家，是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一。

items.en: Hlaford, the ancestor of lord, first meant the keeper of the loaf, the man who fed those who depended on him.
items.cn: lord 的前身 hlaford 最初意为「掌管面包的人」，即供养依附者的男子。

items.en: Middle English joined land and lord into one compound for the man who owned or held land.
items.cn: 中古英语把 land 与 lord 合为一个复合词，指拥有或持有土地的人。

items.en: As more houses were let for rent, landlord widened from the owner of land to the owner of any rented property.
items.cn: 随着越来越多房屋出租，landlord 从土地所有者扩大到任何出租房产的所有者。

items.en: Modern English uses landlord for the person you pay rent to, and keeps the innkeeper sense in older or British pub use.
items.cn: 现代英语用 landlord 指收房租的人，旅店老板义则留在较早用法与英式酒馆说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on land or lord; the near-meaning group collects other words for people who own or manage property.
note.cn: 形近组收由 land 或 lord 构成的词；近义组收其他表示房产所有者或经营者的词。

entries.definition: A woman who owns property and lets it, or runs an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 女房东；女店主。

entries.definition: The system in which landlords take rent from tenants.
entries.definitionCN: 地主向佃户收租的制度。

entries.definition: A master or nobleman, the second half of this compound.
entries.definitionCN: 主人或贵族，是这个词的后一半。

entries.definition: A person who legally possesses something.
entries.definitionCN: 合法拥有某物的人。

entries.definition: The owner of a business or of property.
entries.definitionCN: 企业或房产的所有者。

entries.definition: A person who grants a lease of property.
entries.definitionCN: 出租房产并授予租约的人。

entries.definition: A person who runs an inn.
entries.definitionCN: 经营旅店的人。

normalIntro.en: The compound joins the oldest word for ground to the old word for a master, and its history moves from holding soil to collecting rent.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词把最古老的「土地」一词与古老的「主人」一词结合，其历史从持有土地走向收取租金。

normal.en: Land is the ground itself, one of the oldest Germanic words in English.
normal.cn: land 就是土地本身，是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一。

normal.en: Lord began as hlaford, the keeper of the loaf, the man who fed his household.
normal.cn: lord 起初是 hlaford，即掌管面包、供养一家人的人。

normal.en: Landlord is literally the lord of the land, the man whose word ruled his ground.
normal.cn: landlord 字面就是「土地之主」，他的话在自己地界上说了算。

normal.en: When renting spread, the lord of the land became the man who collects rent, while keeping his keys.
normal.cn: 当租房普及，土地之主变成了收房租的人，钥匙也仍在他手里。

normal.en: Landlady adds the female counterpart, and landlordism names the system rather than a person.
normal.cn: landlady 提供女性对应形式，landlordism 指制度而非某个人。

abstract.en: A compound can carry a whole social order: land plus master equals power over the people who live on it.
abstract.cn: 一个复合词能装下整套社会秩序：土地加主人，等于对住在上面的人的支配权。

abstract.en: The word did not change owners; it changed what owning meant, from soil to rent.
abstract.cn: 这个词换的不是所有者，而是「拥有」的含义：从泥土变为租金。

abstract.en: Keys and rent receipts are the modern costume of an old feudal title.
abstract.cn: 钥匙与房租收据，是一个古老封建头衔的现代装扮。

examples.en: The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
examples.cn: 房东敲门来收房租。

examples.en: She has not paid the landlord this month.
examples.cn: 她这个月还没把房租交给房东。

examples.en: The landlord of the old inn kept a fire burning all winter.
examples.cn: 那家老旅店的老板整个冬天都让炉火不灭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「懒得劳动」——懒得劳动的地主靠收租过日子；谐音记住 landlord 是房东、地主。

root: 由古英语 land（土地）与 lord（前身 hlaford，掌管面包者）复合而成；指拥有土地或出租房产的人。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the man who holds land and lets others use it; from there it names the rent collector, the innkeeper and the feudal lord.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是持有土地并让别人使用的人；由此分出收房租者、旅店老板与封建领主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man at a doorway holding keys and a bundle of rent receipts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在门口，手里拿着钥匙和一沓房租收据。

branches.en: a knock at the door on rent day
branches.cn: 收租日的一次敲门

branches.en: a tenant handing over an envelope of cash
branches.cn: 房客递上一个装现金的信封

branches.en: a manor court settling a dispute
branches.cn: 庄园法庭裁决一场纠纷

branches.en: a fire kept burning in an old inn
branches.cn: 老旅店里整夜不灭的炉火

branches.en: a pub keeper wiping the counter
branches.cn: 酒馆掌柜擦着柜台

intro.en: The word is a Germanic compound of two Old English nouns, and English suffixes later build abstract and feminine forms from it.
intro.cn: 这个词是两个古英语名词组成的日耳曼复合词，后来英语后缀又由它造出抽象名词与女性形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound; both of its parts are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它的两个组成部分都属日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 风景；景观；地貌；（某一领域的）局面；（印刷、摄影）横向版式
definition_en: the visible features of an area of land; a picture representing such scenery; the overall pattern of a field of activity; (printing) a page format wider than it is tall
core_image: 从高处望下去，田野、河流与道路拼成一整幅画
scene: 地理课上，老师把投影切成一幅航拍图。The valley landscape was left behind by a retreating glacier.
sceneCN: 这里 landscape 是「地貌景观」（第 1 个义项：一片土地的可见形态）；句意：这条河谷景观是冰川退却后留下的。

pos.zh: 风景；景观；地貌（可数指一片景观，不可数指景观类型）
（某领域的）局面；横向版式（常带修饰语，如 political landscape）

derivatives.zh: 经景观设计的
景观布置；造景
景观设计师；园林工
海景；海景画
城市景观
月球表面景观

senses.title: Visible features of land
senses.definition: the shape, texture, and features of an area of land, including hills, rivers, fields, and vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 一片土地的形状、质地与特征，包括山丘、河流、田野与植被
senses.example: Glaciers shaped the landscape of this valley.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川塑造了这条河谷的地貌。
senses.why: Landscape is borrowed from Dutch landschap, land plus -schap, a suffix of state or condition cognate with English -ship. The word began as 'the condition of the land', which is why it can name both a region and how that region looks.
senses.whyCN: landscape 借自荷兰语 landschap，由 land 加 -schap 构成，后者是表示状态或状况的后缀，与英语 -ship 同源。这个词最初意为“土地的状况”，所以它既能命名一片区域，也能命名这片区域的样子。

senses.title: A landscape painting
senses.definition: a painting or photograph whose main subject is natural scenery
senses.definitionCN: 以自然景色为主要题材的绘画或摄影
senses.example: The museum bought a seventeenth-century Dutch landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆买下一幅 17 世纪荷兰风景画。
senses.why: The word entered English in the sixteenth century as an art term: a picture of a land. Dutch painters made the genre famous, and the word travelled with the paintings.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 16 世纪作为艺术术语进入英语：一幅关于土地的画。荷兰画家使这一画种闻名，词随画一起传来。

senses.title: Landscape in geography and ecology
senses.titleCN: 地理与生态学中的景观
senses.definition: an area considered as a system of interacting physical, biological, and human features
senses.definitionCN: 被视作物理、生物与人文特征交互系统的区域
senses.example: Landscape ecology studies how patches of habitat connect.
senses.exampleCN: 景观生态学研究栖息地斑块如何连接。
senses.why: Geography turned the word into a technical unit: a landscape is not just a view but a system with boundaries and flows. The visual sense survives inside the scientific one.
senses.whyCN: 地理学把这个词变成技术单位：景观不只是视野，而是有边界与流动的系统。视觉义在科学义内部存活下来。

senses.title: The pattern of a field of activity
senses.definition: the overall arrangement of forces, players, or conditions in a particular area of activity
senses.definitionCN: 某一活动领域中力量、参与者或条件的总体布局
senses.example: The merger changed the competitive landscape of the industry.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并改变了该行业的竞争格局。
senses.why: Twentieth-century business and political writing borrowed the word for a field of play: competitors occupy positions the way hills occupy a view. The metaphor is spatial, and it treats the situation as something seen from above.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的商业与政治写作把这个词借来指一个竞技场：竞争者占据位置，就像山丘占据视野。这个比喻是空间性的，把局势当作从高处看到的东西。

senses.title: Landscape page format
senses.definition: a page or image orientation in which the width is greater than the height
senses.definitionCN: 宽度大于高度的页面或图像方向
senses.example: Print the map in landscape format so the whole route fits.
senses.exampleCN: 把地图打成横向版式，好让整条路线容纳进来。
senses.why: Printing and photography borrowed the word because a wide page resembles a landscape view: the eye moves sideways across it. The term now means orientation alone, with no scenery involved.
senses.whyCN: 印刷与摄影借用这个词，因为宽页面像一幅风景视野：视线横向扫过。这个术语如今只指方向，与景色无关。

senses.title: Landscape design
senses.definition: the planned shaping of gardens, parks, and grounds for use and appearance
senses.definitionCN: 为使用与外观而对花园、公园与场地进行的规划性塑造
senses.example: The landscape of the campus was redesigned last year.
senses.exampleCN: 校园的景观去年被重新设计。
senses.why: Gardening adopted the word in the eighteenth century, when improvers began shaping views rather than merely planting. Landscape became both the object seen and the act of arranging it.
senses.whyCN: 园艺在 18 世纪采用这个词，当时造园者开始塑造视野，而不只是种植。landscape 由此既指被看见的对象，也指安排它的行为。

senses.title: Cultural landscape
senses.definition: a landscape shaped by human activity and carrying the marks of a community's history
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动塑造、带有群体历史印记的景观
senses.example: Rice terraces are a cultural landscape maintained for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 梯田是维护了数百年的文化景观。
senses.why: Heritage studies use the term to reject the split between nature and culture: a landscape is co-produced by people and place. The word then carries a claim about who made what we see.
senses.whyCN: 遗产研究用这个术语来否定自然与文化的截然二分：景观由人与地方共同生产。这个词由此承载一个主张：我们所见的景象是谁造成的。

senses.title: The current overall situation
senses.definition: the general state of affairs that someone surveys before acting
senses.definitionCN: 某人在行动前所审视的总体状况
senses.example: Before launching the product, they studied the regulatory landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 在推出产品之前，他们研究了监管形势。
senses.why: This sense generalises the spatial metaphor to any field: the landscape is what you see when you step back. It implies a survey before a decision, not a detailed analysis of one part.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把空间比喻推广到任何领域：景观是你退后一步看到的东西。它暗示决策前的总体巡视，而不是对某一局部的细致分析。

intro.en: Landscape is a sixteenth-century borrowing from Dutch landschap, land plus -schap (state, condition), cognate with English -ship. It entered English first as a painting term and later spread to geography, gardening, and figurative usage.
intro.cn: landscape 是 16 世纪从荷兰语 landschap 借来的词，由 land 加 -schap（状态、状况）构成，与英语 -ship 同源。它先作为绘画术语进入英语，后来扩展到地理、园艺与比喻用法。

items.en: Dutch landschap combined land with -schap, a suffix of condition or collection, related to English -ship. The word meant 'the condition of the land' or 'a region', not yet a picture.
items.cn: 荷兰语 landschap 把 land 与表示状况或集合的后缀 -schap 结合，后者与英语 -ship 相关。该词意为“土地的状况”或“一片地区”，当时还不是画。

items.en: English borrowed landscape in the sixteenth century as a term for a painting of scenery, alongside the older variant landskip. The artistic sense came first in English usage.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 landscape，作为描绘景色的绘画术语，同时还有较早的变体 landskip。在英语用法中，艺术义最先出现。

items.en: Landscape gardening made the word active: to landscape a park was to arrange its views. The noun and the verb then grew together.
items.cn: 景观造园使这个词变为主动：landscape a park 意为安排它的视野。名词与动词由此一起生长。

items.en: Geography adopted landscape as a technical term for the visible form of a region, studied through maps and fieldwork. Physical and cultural landscapes were distinguished.
items.cn: 地理学采用 landscape 作为区域可见形态的技术术语，通过地图与野外工作研究。自然景观与文化景观被区分开来。

items.en: Business, politics, and journalism extended the word to any field of activity, producing phrases such as 'the competitive landscape'. The spatial metaphor became a standard way to describe strategy.
items.cn: 商业、政治与新闻把这个词扩展到任何活动领域，产生 the competitive landscape 等说法。空间比喻成为描述战略的标准方式。

items.en: Printing and photography borrowed landscape for a page wider than it is tall, because such a page resembles a wide view. The term now names orientation alone.
items.cn: 印刷与摄影借用 landscape 指宽大于高的页面，因为这样的页面像一幅宽视野。这个术语如今只命名方向。

note.en: The look-alike group separates words sharing the -scape suffix or the land element but built on different bases; the near-meaning group separates scenery, terrain, and view.
note.cn: 形近组区分共享 -scape 后缀或 land 成分但基词不同的词；近义组区分 scenery、terrain 与 view。

entries.definition: a view or picture of the sea. It is a modern formation on the model of landscape, replacing land with sea.
entries.definitionCN: 海景或海景画。它是仿 landscape 构成的现代词，把 land 换成 sea。

entries.definition: someone blamed for others' faults. The scape here comes from escape, not from landscape's -schap; the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 替他人受责的人。这里的 scape 来自 escape，而非 landscape 的 -schap；相似纯属偶然。

entries.definition: the sliding down of earth or rock, or an overwhelming election victory. It joins land with slide, with no sense of scenery.
entries.definitionCN: 土石滑落，或压倒性的选举胜利。它把 land 与 slide 结合，与景色无关。

entries.definition: the general appearance of a place, especially when attractive. It is uncountable and evaluative; landscape can be neutral and countable.
entries.definitionCN: 一个地方的整体外观，尤指宜人时。它不可数且带评价；landscape 可中性、可数。

entries.definition: the physical surface of land, especially as it affects movement. It stresses ground conditions, while landscape includes what is seen.
entries.definitionCN: 土地的物理表面，尤指影响行进时。它强调地面条件，而 landscape 包含所见之物。

entries.definition: what can be seen from a particular place. It depends on the observer's position; a landscape exists as a region, whether or not anyone is looking.
entries.definitionCN: 从某一地点能看到的东西。它取决于观察者的位置；landscape 作为区域存在，无论是否有人在看。

normalIntro.en: Real associations: Dutch landschap, the -ship suffix, the painting term of the sixteenth century, and the modern phrase political landscape.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联想：荷兰语 landschap、-ship 后缀、16 世纪的绘画术语，以及现代说法 political landscape。

normal.en: land + -schap (the same suffix as -ship): landscape is 'the condition of the land'.
normal.cn: land + -schap（与 -ship 同源的后缀）：landscape 就是“土地的状况”。

normal.en: It entered English as a painting word, which is why a landscape can be a picture as well as a place.
normal.cn: 它作为绘画词进入英语，所以 landscape 既可是地方，也可是画。

normal.en: A wide page is printed in landscape because it looks like a wide view.
normal.cn: 宽页面以横向打印，因为它看起来像一幅宽视野。

normal.en: 'Political landscape' treats parties as hills occupying positions in a view.
normal.cn: political landscape 把政党当作占据视野中位置的山丘。

normal.en: seascape and cityscape are modern copies of the same pattern.
normal.cn: seascape 与 cityscape 是同一模式的现代仿造词。

abstract.en: The suffix means condition, not picture: the word is about how land stands, and the picture is a later use.
abstract.cn: 后缀意为状况，而非图画：这个词关乎土地处于何种状态，图画是后来的用法。

abstract.en: Every figurative landscape invites you to step back — the word always implies a viewing distance.
abstract.cn: 每一个比喻性的 landscape 都邀请你退后一步——这个词总暗示一段观看距离。

abstract.en: A cultural landscape denies the split between nature and human history: what you see was co-produced.
abstract.cn: 文化景观否定自然与人类历史的二分：你所见的是共同生产的。

examples.en: The volcanic landscape attracts hikers from around the world.
examples.cn: 这片火山地貌吸引着世界各地的徒步者。

examples.en: The election reshaped the political landscape of the country.
examples.cn: 这次选举重塑了该国的政治格局。

examples.en: The map is printed in landscape so that the coastline fits on one page.
examples.cn: 地图以横向版式印制，好让海岸线容纳在一页内。

dict_mnemonic.text: “兰德斯给普”——荷兰的兰德斯（Land）把土地的样子“给”了出来 → landscape 风景、景观

root: 荷兰语 landschap = land（土地）+ -schap（状态、状况，与英语 -ship 同源）；字面义“土地的状况”，核心是“从远处看到的一片土地的形态与格局”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of landscape all describe a wide arrangement seen as a whole: terrain, a painting, an ecological system, a field of competition, a page, a designed garden, a human-shaped heritage, and the current situation. The word always implies a viewing distance.
sensesIntro.cn: landscape 的八个义项都描述被当作整体看待的宽广布局：地貌、绘画、生态系统、竞争场域、页面、设计的园林、人塑造的遗产，以及当前形势。这个词总暗示一段观看距离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a high vantage point where fields, a river, and roads compose one picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：一处高处的视点，田野、河流与道路组成一幅画。

branches.en: NATURE: terrain and ecological systems are landscapes as regions, not merely as views.
branches.cn: 自然：地貌与生态系统作为区域性的景观，而不只是视野。

branches.en: ART AND DESIGN: painting and garden-making both arrange what will be seen.
branches.cn: 艺术与设计：绘画与造园都在安排将被看到的东西。

branches.en: SITUATION: fields of activity are surveyed from above and described as layouts.
branches.cn: 形势：活动领域被从高处巡视，并被描述为布局。

branches.en: FORMAT: a wide page borrows the shape of a wide view.
branches.cn: 版式：宽页面借用了宽视野的形状。

branches.en: HERITAGE: a cultural landscape denies the split between nature and human history.
branches.cn: 遗产：文化景观否定自然与人类历史的二分。

intro.en: Landscape is Dutch landschap, land + -schap, cognate with English -ship. The suffix has become productive in English: seascape, cityscape, and moonscape are modern coinages on the same pattern.
intro.cn: landscape 是荷兰语 landschap，由 land + -schap 构成，与英语 -ship 同源。这个后缀在英语中变得能产：seascape、cityscape、moonscape 都是按同一模式造的现代词。

latinIntro.en: Landscape has no Latin root: it is a Germanic compound of land and -schap. The nearest Latin relatives in English vocabulary are terra 'land' and campus 'field', which supply terrain and campus, but they are not etymological relatives.
latinIntro.cn: landscape 没有拉丁词根：它是 land 与 -schap 的日耳曼语复合词。英语词汇中最近的拉丁亲属是 terra“土地”与 campus“田野”，它们提供 terrain 与 campus，但并非词源亲属。

items.meaning: the visible form of a region; a picture of it
items.example: The landscape changed after the flood.

items.meaningCN: 经景观设计的（-ed 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 酒店有经过设计的园林。

items.meaningCN: 景观布置；造景（-ing 构成名词）
items.exampleCN: 景观布置提升了房产价值。

items.meaningCN: 景观设计师；园林工（-er 表施动者）
items.exampleCN: 景观设计师种下本地草类。

items.meaning: a view or picture of the sea
the visual character of a city
items.example: The cityscape is dominated by glass towers.
items.exampleCN: 城市景观以玻璃塔楼为主。

items.meaningCN: 月球表面景观；荒凉地貌（moon + -scape）
items.example: The mining site resembled a moonscape.
items.exampleCN: 矿区看起来像月球表面。

items.meaning: the solid surface of the earth
items.meaningCN: 土地；陆地（古英语本族词）
items.example: The land rises toward the hills.

items.meaningCN: 风景画（古旧变体，今已罕用）
items.exampleCN: 清单上列有两幅风景画。

definition_zh: 小路；小巷；车道；泳道；航线
definition_en: a narrow road or path; one of the marked strips of a road, track or pool; a fixed route used by ships or aircraft
core_image: 村口一条窄路，两旁是石墙和伸出来的树枝
scene: 雨后的村子很安静，一条窄巷两边的石墙被淋得发亮。She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
sceneCN: 这里是「小路、小巷」（第 1 个义项：狭窄的道路）；句意是她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。图中可辨识物件：石墙、湿路面、树枝。

pos.zh: 小路；小巷；车道；泳道；航线

derivatives.zh: 由 lane 与 way 复合而成，义为「小巷；巷道」
由 multi- 与 lane 复合而成，义为「多车道的」
由 two 与 lane 复合而成，义为「双车道的」

senses.title: A narrow road or path
senses.definition: a narrow road, especially one in the countryside or between buildings
senses.definitionCN: 狭窄的道路，尤指乡间或建筑物之间的小路
senses.example: She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。
senses.why: Old English lane named a narrow path, and narrowness remains the clearest feature of this sense.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 lane 指狭窄的小路，而「窄」至今仍是这个义项最鲜明的特征。

senses.title: A marked strip of a road
senses.definition: one of the marked strips into which a road is divided for traffic
senses.definitionCN: 道路为车辆行驶而划分出的标线通道之一
senses.example: The truck moved into the left lane to pass the slower car.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车驶入左侧车道，超过那辆开得较慢的车。
senses.why: Once roads were painted and divided, the old word for a narrow path was ready-made for a narrow strip of traffic.
senses.whyCN: 道路画上线并划分之后，原指窄路的旧词正好用来指窄窄的一条车行道。

senses.title: A marked strip of a track or pool
senses.definition: one of the parallel strips used for racing on a track or in a swimming pool
senses.definitionCN: 田径场或游泳池中供比赛使用的平行分道
senses.example: He swam in the outside lane during the race.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛时他在最外侧的泳道里游。
senses.why: A pool is divided into parallel strips so that swimmers do not collide, and each strip is a narrow path of water.
senses.whyCN: 泳池被分成平行的条带，避免游泳者相互碰撞，而每一条带都是水上的一条窄路。

senses.title: A fixed route for ships or aircraft
senses.definition: a fixed route that ships or aircraft regularly follow
senses.definitionCN: 船只或飞机固定沿用的路线
senses.example: Ships follow a busy lane across the strait.
senses.exampleCN: 船只沿着一条繁忙的航道穿过海峡。
senses.why: A route is also a long narrow strip on a map, so lane extends naturally from a path on land to a path at sea or in the air.
senses.whyCN: 航线在地图上同样是一条狭长的带，所以 lane 从陆上小路自然延伸到海上或空中的路线。

intro.en: Lane is a Germanic word for a narrow path; English has kept the narrowness and applied it to traffic, races and sea routes.
intro.cn: lane 是日耳曼语中指窄路的词；英语保留了「窄」的特征，并把它用到车道、赛道和航线。

items.en: The word is Germanic in origin; a related form is reconstructed, but its exact shape is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，可重构出相关形式，但确切形态并不确定。

items.en: Old English lane meant a narrow path or road, often one between hedges or fields.
items.cn: 古英语 lane 指狭窄的小路，常是树篱或田地之间的一条路。

items.en: Middle English kept lane for country paths and for the narrow streets of a town.
items.cn: 中古英语用 lane 指乡间小路和城里的窄街。

items.en: With modern roads and racing, lane was applied to marked strips of traffic, tracks and pools.
items.cn: 随着现代道路与赛事的出现，lane 被用来指标出的车道、跑道和泳道。

items.en: Modern English also uses lane for fixed shipping and air routes.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 lane 指固定的航线和航道。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and one sound-alike; the near-meaning group collects other narrow ways through space.
note.cn: 形近组收复合词和一个同音词；近义组收其他穿越空间的狭窄道路。

entries.definition: The past participle of lie, as in having lain down; it sounds the same but belongs to a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词 lie 的过去分词，如「已经躺下」；它与 lane 同音，但属于另一个动词。

entries.definition: A narrow passage or service road, common in Australian and New Zealand English.
entries.definitionCN: 狭窄的通道或服务性小路，常见于澳大利亚与新西兰英语。

entries.definition: Tall and thin in an awkward way; only the spelling is close, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 瘦高而显得笨拙的；只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Having several marked strips for traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有数条标线车道的。

entries.definition: A narrow passage between or behind buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑物之间或后方的一条窄通道。

entries.definition: A track worn by feet or made for walking.
entries.definitionCN: 被人踩出或专为行走而修的小径。

entries.definition: A wide way for vehicles, usually much broader than a lane.
entries.definitionCN: 供车辆行驶的宽阔道路，通常比 lane 宽得多。

entries.definition: A rough path or a prepared course for racing.
entries.definitionCN: 崎岖的小路，或为比赛修整好的跑道。

normalIntro.en: The word stays tied to narrowness; compounds count strips, and the same shape is read on roads, pools and maps.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词始终与「窄」相连；复合词数出条带的数量，而同样的形状在道路、泳池和地图上都能看到。

normal.en: Old English lane meant a narrow path, which is why a country lane is still narrower than a road.
normal.cn: 古英语 lane 指窄路，所以乡间 lane 至今仍比 road 窄。

normal.en: Lain is a homophone but not a relative: it is the past participle of lie, meaning to rest flat.
normal.cn: lain 是同音词而不是同族词：它是 lie 的过去分词，意为平躺。

normal.en: Laneway adds way to lane, and it is the usual word for a narrow service passage in Australasian English.
normal.cn: laneway 在 lane 后加 way，是澳新英语中表示狭窄通道的常用词。

normal.en: Multi-lane and two-lane count the marked strips, so the compound tells you how many streams of traffic there are.
normal.cn: multi-lane 和 two-lane 数的是标线通道，所以复合词直接说明有几股车流。

normal.en: A bus lane is a marked strip reserved for buses, which shows how far lane has moved from a country path.
normal.cn: bus lane 是留给公交车的标线通道，由此可见 lane 已从乡间小路走出多远。

abstract.en: A lane is a line cut through space, whether grass, asphalt or water, and that is why one word serves all of them.
abstract.cn: lane 是在空间里划出的一条线，无论在草地、柏油还是水面上，所以一个词能服务所有这些场景。

abstract.en: Narrowness separates a lane from a road, just as a single track separates one life from another.
abstract.cn: 窄，把 lane 与 road 区分开，就像单条轨迹把一种人生与另一种分开。

abstract.en: Down memory lane shows that a path can also run through time rather than through land.
abstract.cn: down memory lane 说明道路也可以穿过时间，而不只是穿过土地。

examples.en: She walked down a quiet lane lined with old stone walls.
examples.cn: 她沿着一条两旁是旧石墙的安静小巷走着。

examples.en: The truck moved into the left lane to pass the slower car.
examples.cn: 卡车驶入左侧车道，超过那辆开得较慢的车。

examples.en: He swam in the outside lane during the race.
examples.cn: 比赛时他在最外侧的泳道里游。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「雷恩」——人名雷恩总爱走乡间小路；lane 是小路。

root: 古英语 lane，属日耳曼语固有词，指狭窄的道路；与拉丁语无可靠同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Narrow passage is the core; it widens into traffic strips, racing strips and routes drawn across sea or sky.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是狭窄的通道；它扩展成车道、赛道，以及画在海面或天空上的航线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow path between two stone walls, just wide enough for one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：两道石墙之间的一条窄路，只容一人走过。

branches.en: a country path with hedges on both sides
branches.cn: 两旁是树篱的乡间小路

branches.en: a town passage too narrow for two carts
branches.cn: 窄得容不下两辆马车的城中通道

branches.en: painted lines splitting a wide road
branches.cn: 把宽路分开的油漆标线

branches.en: ropes floating across a swimming pool
branches.cn: 横在泳池里的浮标绳

branches.en: a dotted route drawn across a chart of the sea
branches.cn: 在海图上画出的一条虚线航线

intro.en: A Germanic noun forms one compound with way, one prefix compound with multi-, and one counting compound with two.
intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词分别与 way、前缀 multi- 和数词 two 组成复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a narrow road or marked strip
a narrow road in the countryside

definition_zh: 语言；言语；（某一领域的）表达方式；计算机语言
definition_en: a system of spoken or written signs used for communication, or a particular style or code of expression
core_image: 一张围着许多人的旧木桌，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页，几个人正用手势和声音相互回应
scene: 旧木桌旁围坐着来自几座村镇的人，桌上摊着写满不同文字的纸页。Language was the only tool they had in common that afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里指「用于交流的声音与符号系统」（第 1 个义项：人类交流的整体系统）；句意为那天下午，语言是他们唯一共同拥有的工具。可辨识物件：旧木桌、纸页、不同文字、手势。

pos.zh: 语言；言语；表达方式（可数与不可数两用）

derivatives.zh: 语言的；语言学的
语言学
语言学家
多语的
双语的 / 双语者

senses.title: The human system of communication
senses.titleCN: 人类用于交流的符号系统
senses.definition: the shared system of sounds, words and grammar by which people communicate
senses.definitionCN: 人们借以交流的声音、词汇与语法的共享系统
senses.example: Language is learned in company, not from a dictionary alone.
senses.exampleCN: 语言是在与人相处中学到的，而不是只靠词典。
senses.why: the word came from the Latin name for the tongue, so the oldest image is the organ that produces speech.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自拉丁语对「舌头」的称呼，因此最古老的画面是发出言语的器官。

senses.title: A particular named tongue
senses.definition: a specific system such as Chinese, Arabic or Swahili, counted as one item
senses.definitionCN: 如汉语、阿拉伯语或斯瓦希里语等具体系统，可作为一个单位计数
senses.example: She speaks four languages and reads two more.
senses.exampleCN: 她会说四种语言，还能读另外两种。
senses.why: once the general capacity was recognized, each separate system needed the same name.
senses.whyCN: 当整体能力被认出之后，每一个独立的系统也需要同一个名称。

senses.title: Speech as it is actually used
senses.definition: the spoken words of a person or group on a given occasion, as opposed to writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某群体在某一场合说出的具体话语，与书面语相对
senses.example: His language in the meeting was far plainer than his letters.
senses.exampleCN: 他在会上说的话比他的书信朴素得多。
senses.why: the tongue is the instrument of speech, so the word also names the spoken output itself.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是说话的器官，因此这个词也指说出来的产物。

senses.title: The style and wording of a text
senses.definition: the choice of words and sentence patterns that gives a text its tone
senses.definitionCN: 使文本形成某种语气的用词与句式选择
senses.example: The language of the report was careful but cold.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告的措辞谨慎而冷淡。
senses.why: a text's manner of speech can be described with the same word used for a nation's tongue.
senses.whyCN: 一个文本的说话方式，可以用描述民族语言的同一个词来指称。

senses.title: The vocabulary of a special field
senses.titleCN: 某一专业的行话与术语
senses.definition: the technical words and conventions used by a profession or subject
senses.definitionCN: 某职业或学科使用的术语与惯例
senses.example: Legal language keeps ordinary readers at a distance.
senses.exampleCN: 法律行话把普通读者挡在门外。
senses.why: a profession speaks its own tongue, so its terms are called a language.
senses.whyCN: 一个职业说自己的话，因此其术语被称作一种语言。

senses.title: A code for machines
senses.definition: a formal set of instructions that a computer can process
senses.definitionCN: 计算机可以处理的一套形式化指令
senses.example: The course teaches one programming language at a time.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课一次只教一种编程语言。
senses.why: the word was extended to any rule-governed code, including one no human speaks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词被扩展到任何有规则的代码，包括没有人说的那种。

senses.title: Non-verbal signals
senses.definition: meaning carried by gesture, posture or tone rather than words
senses.definitionCN: 由手势、姿态或语气而非词语承载的意义
senses.example: Her body language said more than her answer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的肢体语言比回答说明了更多。
senses.why: meaning is carried without the tongue at all, and the word follows the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 意义完全不经舌头而传递，词也跟着意义走。

senses.title: The human capacity for speech
senses.titleCN: 人类拥有语言的天赋能力
senses.definition: the general human ability to acquire and use a grammar, studied as a faculty
senses.definitionCN: 人类习得并使用语法的总体能力，被当作一种官能来研究
senses.example: Language separates human communication from simple signalling.
senses.exampleCN: 语言使人类交流区别于简单的信号传递。
senses.why: the most abstract sense returns to the original faculty that makes every other sense possible.
senses.whyCN: 最抽象的义项回到那项使其他所有义项成为可能的原初官能。

intro.en: Language comes from Old French langage, from Latin lingua 'tongue, language'. The further origin of lingua is not established. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个词来自古法语 langage，再上溯拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」。lingua 更早的来源未获证明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lingua meant both 'tongue' and 'language'. The sense grew from the organ to what the organ produces, a common pattern in many languages.
items.cn: lingua 兼指「舌头」与「语言」。词义从器官转到器官的产物，这在许多语言中都是常见模式。

items.en: The deeper origin of lingua is unsettled. A link sometimes proposed with a verb meaning 'to lick' is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: lingua 更深的来源没有定论。有人提出它与一个表「舔」的动词有关，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French langage named speech and the way one speaks; English borrowed it in the age of Norman rule.
items.cn: 古法语 langage 指言语及说话方式；英语在诺曼统治时期借入。

items.en: Middle English used the word for a nation's tongue and for a person's manner of speech, both senses surviving today.
items.cn: 中古英语用这个词指一个民族的语言，也指个人的说话方式，两义都留存至今。

items.en: Modern technical life extended the word to formal codes, giving programming languages, and to gesture, giving body language.
items.cn: 现代技术生活把词扩展到形式化代码，产生「编程语言」，也扩展到姿态，产生「肢体语言」。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested pre-Latin form of lingua is agreed, and the exact route through French is reconstructed from later records.
items.cn: 来源不确定：lingua 在拉丁语之前的形式没有公认书证，经法语传入的确切路径亦由较晚记录构拟。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same root that are often confused; group two holds near neighbours that name communication.
note.cn: 第一组是同根而常被混淆的词；第二组是表示交流的近义词。

entries.definition: Describes what relates to language; it never names the system itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述与语言有关的性质，本身不指那套系统。

entries.definition: The scientific study of language, not a language and not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指对语言的科学研究，既不是一种语言，也不是一个人。

entries.definition: A person who studies language, or loosely one who knows several.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究语言的人，或宽泛地指通晓多种语言的人。

entries.definition: An informal word for a foreign language or a jargon; it is playful where language is neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 指外语或行话的口语说法，语气戏谑，而「语言」一词为中性。

entries.definition: The act or occasion of speaking; it covers sound but not writing or the abstract system.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话的行为或场合，覆盖声音，却不含书面语或抽象系统。

entries.definition: An old word for a language, as in the mother tongue; it is close but archaic in most uses.
entries.definitionCN: 指语言的旧说法，如「母语」；意思接近，但多数用法已古旧。

entries.definition: One variety within a language; calling it a language is a political judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 指一种语言内部的变体；称它为「语言」常是政治判断。

entries.definition: Any system of signs with rules, including machines; it lacks the human and social weight of language.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何有规则的符号系统，包括机器；缺少语言的人类与社会分量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实相关词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'tongue', so the word begins as the body part that makes speech.
normal.cn: 词根意为「舌头」，因此这个词最初就是制造言语的身体部位。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the range: foreign language, body language, programming language.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出范围：外语、肢体语言、编程语言。

normal.en: The adjective, the discipline and the person all come from the same root.
normal.cn: 形容词、学科与人都出自同一词根。

normal.en: The family runs linguistic, linguistics, linguist, multilingual, bilingual.
normal.cn: 同族包括「语言的」「语言学」「语言学家」「多语的」「双语的」。

normal.en: Counting languages uses the plural, speaking in general uses the singular.
normal.cn: 数具体语言用复数，泛指说话能力用单数。

abstract.en: Picture a table where every sheet is written in a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，每张纸都出自不同的笔迹。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built from sounds rather than stones.
abstract.cn: 想象一座用声音而非石头搭成的桥。

abstract.en: Picture a key ring that opens a different door for every listener.
abstract.cn: 想象一串钥匙，对每个听者打开不同的一扇门。

examples.en: Language changes faster in cities than in isolated valleys.
examples.cn: 语言在城市里的变化比在封闭山谷中更快。

examples.en: The two communities share a border but not a language.
examples.cn: 这两个社群共享一条边界，却不共享一种语言。

examples.en: Nurses are trained to read the body language of anxious patients.
examples.cn: 护士受过训练，能读懂焦虑病人的肢体语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「兰格维吉」——拦住陌生人开口，靠的就是这套声音与符号的系统。

root: 拉丁 lingua「舌头、语言」经古法语 langage 进入英语；词义由器官转向器官的产物。lingua 更深来源不确定，与表「舔」动词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one organ: the tongue produces speech, speech becomes a named system, that system takes styles and jargons, and the same word is finally lent to machines and to silent gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个器官铺开：舌头产生言语，言语成为具名的系统，系统又生出风格与行话，最后同一个词被借给机器与无声的姿态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table, many scripts, and hands answering in gesture and sound.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子、多种文字，人们用手势与声音相互回应。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: the human faculty and its shared system are the two sides of one coin.
branches.cn: 能力：人类的官能与共享系统是同一枚硬币的两面。

branches.en: COUNTED TONGUES: each separate system can be named and counted.
branches.cn: 可数的语言：每一套独立系统都可被命名与计数。

branches.en: BEYOND WORDS: actual speech and silent gesture both carry meaning.
branches.cn: 超出词语：实际说出的话与无声的姿态都承载意义。

branches.en: TONE OF A TEXT: word choice alone can make writing warm or cold.
branches.cn: 文本的语气：仅靠选词就能让文字变暖或变冷。

branches.en: RULED CODES: a profession's jargon and a machine's instructions are both governed sets.
branches.cn: 有规则的代码：专业行话与机器指令都是受规则支配的集合。

intro.en: The word is a French-shaped noun built on a Latin root meaning 'tongue', and that root also builds the whole linguistic family.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语成形的名词，建在拉丁语表「舌头」的词根上，这个词根也构成整个「语言」词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin lingua gives language, linguist and linguistics through French and Latin endings; the same root appears in the adjective for 'tongue-shaped'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lingua 经法语与拉丁词尾衍生出「语言」「语言学家」与「语言学」；同一词根也出现在表「舌形」的形容词里。

items.meaning: the organ of speech, and speech itself
items.example: The root already carries both the body part and its product.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根已同时带着器官与其产物。

items.example: Language is older than any dictionary.
items.exampleCN: 语言比任何词典都古老。

items.example: The linguist recorded the last speakers.
items.exampleCN: 这位语言学家记录了最后的说话者。
语言证据为这份文本定了年代。
语言学成为一门大学学科。

items.example: Bilingual signs appeared at the airport.

items.exampleCN: 这座城市以多语并存为荣。

items.example: The manual is full of technical lingo.
items.exampleCN: 这本手册满是技术行话。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 双舌的；使用两种语言的

definition_zh: 大的；大型的；大量的；广泛的
definition_en: big in size, amount or importance, or broad in range
core_image: 一双手在身前比出一个很宽的圆，几乎抱不过来
scene: 仓库门被推开，里面堆着一人多高的木箱。A large shipment of rice arrived at the port.
sceneCN: 这里是「大量的、大批的」（第 2 个义项：指数量或规模大）；句意为一大批大米运抵港口。图中可辨识物件：仓库门、堆叠的木箱、货运单。

derivatives.zh: 由 large 加 -ly 构成，义为「大部分；主要地」
由 en- 加 large 构成，义为「扩大；放大」
由 large 经法语 largesse 而来，义为「慷慨；施赠」
由 large 加 -ish 构成，义为「相当大的」

senses.title: Big in physical size
senses.definition: big in size or dimensions compared with others of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类相比在尺寸或体积上很大
senses.example: They moved into a large house near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬进了河边一栋大房子。
senses.why: Large came from a Latin word for abundance, so its first English sense is simply 'much in size'.
senses.whyCN: large 来自一个表示「丰足」的拉丁词，所以它最早在英语里就是「尺寸上很大」。

senses.title: Great in amount or scale
senses.definition: great in number, amount or extent, as in a large shipment or a large sum
senses.definitionCN: 在数量、金额或规模上很大，如大批货物或大笔款项
senses.example: A large shipment of rice arrived at the port.
senses.exampleCN: 一大批大米运抵港口。
senses.why: From size the word moves easily to amount: what takes up much space often also comes in great quantity.
senses.whyCN: 从体积很容易转到数量：占地方多的东西，往往数量也大。

senses.title: Broad in range or importance
senses.definition: wide in scope, importance or influence rather than in physical size
senses.definitionCN: 在范围、重要性或影响上广，而不是体积大
senses.example: The decision has a large effect on small businesses.
senses.exampleCN: 这项决定对小企业有重大影响。
senses.why: A wide circle is also a wide reach, so large extends from space to influence and significance.
senses.whyCN: 一个很大的圆也是很大的覆盖范围，于是 large 从空间扩展到影响与重要性。

senses.title: Not confined; at liberty
senses.definition: free from confinement, especially in the fixed phrase at large
senses.definitionCN: 不受拘禁，尤用于固定说法 at large
senses.example: The escaped prisoner is still at large.
senses.exampleCN: 那名逃犯仍在逃。
senses.why: At large once meant 'at liberty, without limits'; the phrase keeps the old sense of a space with no walls.
senses.whyCN: at large 早先意为「自由、没有限制」，这个短语保留了「没有围墙的空间」这一旧义。

intro.en: Large came into English through French from a Latin word meaning abundant and generous, and it kept both size and generosity for a while.
intro.cn: large 经法语进入英语，源头是意为「丰足、慷慨」的拉丁词，曾同时保留「大」与「慷慨」两层意思。

items.en: Largus meant abundant, plentiful and generous, a word about giving much rather than about size alone.
items.cn: largus 意为丰足的、充裕的、慷慨的，重点在「给得多」，而不只是尺寸。

items.en: Old French large kept the sense of wide, generous and abundant.
items.cn: 古法语 large 保留宽广、慷慨、丰足的意思。

items.en: Middle English large covers breadth, generosity and physical size at once.
items.cn: 中古英语的 large 同时覆盖宽广、慷慨与体积大。

items.en: By the fourteenth century the everyday sense of big in size is firmly established.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，「尺寸大」的日常义已经稳固确立。

items.en: Modern English keeps the size sense and preserves the older freedom sense in at large.
items.cn: 现代英语保留尺寸义，并在 at large 中保存了较早的「自由」义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers size words from big to enormous.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干构成的词；近义组收从 big 到 enormous 的尺寸词。

entries.definition: Mostly, or to a great extent.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分；主要地。

entries.definition: To make or become bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 扩大；放大。

entries.definition: Generous giving of money or gifts.
entries.definitionCN: 慷慨；施赠。

entries.definition: Fairly large.
entries.definitionCN: 相当大的。

entries.definition: Of great size, the most general word.
entries.definitionCN: 大的，最通用的词。

entries.definition: Extremely large.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的。

entries.definition: Covering a large area or range.
entries.definitionCN: 广阔的；广泛的。

entries.definition: Large in amount or importance.
entries.definitionCN: 大量的；重大的。

normalIntro.en: The word is short but its family is wide, and the old sense of generosity still hides in one phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词很短，但同族很广，古老的「慷慨」义还藏在一个短语里。

normal.en: Large takes -ly to become largely, meaning mostly.
normal.cn: large 加 -ly 成为 largely，意为「大部分」。

normal.en: Enlarge adds en- 'make' and means to make large.
normal.cn: enlarge 加 en-（使……），意为「使变大」。

normal.en: At large keeps an old sense: free, not confined.
normal.cn: at large 保留旧义：自由、不受拘束。

normal.en: Irregular comparison: large, larger, largest.
normal.cn: 不规则比较：large、larger、largest。

normal.en: By and large is a fixed phrase meaning 'generally speaking'.
normal.cn: by and large 是固定短语，意为「总的来说」。

abstract.en: A word born from generosity reminds us that size and giving were once the same idea.
abstract.cn: 一个从「慷慨」诞生的词提醒人：大小与给予曾是同一个观念。

abstract.en: Large measures space, amount and influence, three scales that rarely agree.
abstract.cn: large 同时衡量空间、数量与影响，这三种尺度很少一致。

abstract.en: At large shows how a phrase can keep an older meaning alive after the word itself has moved on.
abstract.cn: at large 说明短语能在词本身往前走之后，把旧义保存下来。

examples.en: They moved into a large house near the river.
examples.cn: 他们搬进了河边一栋大房子。

examples.en: A large shipment of rice arrived at the port.
examples.cn: 一大批大米运抵港口。

examples.en: The escaped prisoner is still at large.
examples.cn: 那名逃犯仍在逃。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉齐」——把东西拉齐排成一大片，就是 large。

root: 拉丁语 largus（丰足、慷慨）经古法语 large 进入英语；同族词多与「大、宽、给得多」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a wide, abundant extent; it moves from physical size to amount, to influence, and finally to freedom from limits.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「宽而丰足的范围」；义项从体积转到数量，再到影响，最后到不受限制的自由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands drawing a circle so wide that they can hardly reach around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手在身前比出一个宽得几乎抱不过来的圆。

branches.en: a house that fills the width of the lane
branches.cn: 占满小巷宽度的大房子

branches.en: a shipment stacked higher than a person
branches.cn: 堆得比人还高的货物

branches.en: a decision that reaches every small shop
branches.cn: 影响每家小店的决策

branches.en: a prisoner with no walls around him
branches.cn: 身边没有围墙的囚犯

branches.en: size that becomes reach
branches.cn: 变成影响力的尺寸

intro.en: A Latin adjective of abundance, a French reshaping, and three English suffixes carry the family.
intro.cn: 一个表示丰足的拉丁形容词、一次法语改造，以及三个英语后缀支撑起这个词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分地；在很大程度上；（古）慷慨地
definition_en: mainly or for the most part, and to a great extent; an older sense of generously survives in literary use
core_image: 天平的一端压得很低，说明几乎所有重量都落在这一边
scene: 统计报告发布后，记者们围在发言人身边提问。The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
sceneCN: 这里 largely 指「大部分地、主要地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为结果被宣读时人群大体上保持沉默。图中可辨识物件：发布台、话筒、记者的笔记本。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分地；在很大程度上

derivatives.zh: largely 的原级，源自拉丁语 largus，义为「大的；大量的」
由 large 加 -ness 构成，义为「巨大；宽广」
由 en- 加 large 构成，义为「扩大；放大」

senses.title: Mainly, for the most part
senses.definition: in the main, so that most of something is true or affected
senses.definitionCN: 总体上，指某事物的大部分为真或大部分受到影响
senses.example: The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果被宣读时，人群大体上保持沉默。
senses.why: The adverb grew from a word for abundance, so largely counts the greater part of a whole rather than measuring one point on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词来自表示「充裕」的词，所以 largely 数的是整体的较大部分，而不是在刻度上量某一点。

senses.title: To a great extent
senses.definition: to a high degree, so that something is greatly influenced or explained by a cause
senses.definitionCN: 达到很高的程度，指某事很大程度上受某原因影响或由它解释
senses.example: His early success was largely due to the people who taught him.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的成功很大程度上归功于教过他的人。
senses.why: If most of a result comes from one source, that source acts to a great extent, which is how the proportion sense turns into a degree sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个结果大部分来自某一个来源，这个来源就起了很大的作用，于是「比例」义自然转成「程度」义。

senses.title: Generously, in abundance
senses.definition: in a generous or plentiful way, an older literary sense still found in older texts
senses.definitionCN: 以慷慨或丰足的方式，是旧时文学中仍可见到的较早义项
senses.example: The old lord gave largely to the poor of his village.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老领主对村里的穷人施舍很慷慨。
senses.why: Latin largus meant generous as well as abundant, and the earliest English adverb kept that open hand before the sense narrowed to mainly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 largus 既指充裕也指慷慨，最早的英语副词保留了那只张开的手，后来词义才收窄为「主要地」。

intro.en: Largely is the adverb of large, whose Latin source meant generous and abundant before French gave it the sense of broad.
intro.cn: largely 是 large 的副词形式；large 的拉丁来源本指慷慨、充裕，后来法语才赋予它「宽广」的意思。

items.en: Largus meant abundant, generous and free in giving, with little idea of physical size at first.
items.cn: largus 意为充裕、慷慨、乐于给予，起初几乎不含物理大小的意思。

items.en: Old French large kept the Latin word and added the sense of wide or broad, so size entered the meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 large 承接拉丁词义，又加上「宽、阔」的意思，于是大小进入了词义。

items.en: Middle English large covered both generosity and breadth, and the adverb largely was built with -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语 large 同时含慷慨与宽广，副词 largely 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Largely first meant in a generous or plentiful manner, then drifted towards for the greater part.
items.cn: largely 最初意为「慷慨地、大量地」，后来转向「大部分地」。

items.en: Modern English uses largely almost only for mainly or to a great extent, while the generous sense survives in literary or older use.
items.cn: 现代英语的 largely 几乎只表示「主要地、在很大程度上」，慷慨义只留在文学或较早用法中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the large family and its adverbs; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of proportion.
note.cn: 形近组收 large 一词族及其副词；近义组收其他表示比例的副词。

entries.definition: Big in size or amount, the adjective behind largely.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量大的，是 largely 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放大、扩大。

entries.definition: The quality of being large.
entries.definitionCN: 大的性质；巨大。

entries.definition: For the most part, more than anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分地；首要地。

entries.definition: Usually or in most cases.
entries.definitionCN: 通常；大多数情况下。

entries.definition: Mainly, above all other things.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，首要地。

entries.definition: Over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛地；在许多地方或许多人中。

normalIntro.en: The adverb counts the bigger part of a whole, and its Latin root still remembers generosity.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词数的是整体中较大的那一部分，它的拉丁词根还记着「慷慨」。

normal.en: Large comes from Latin largus, which meant generous and plentiful before it meant big.
normal.cn: large 来自拉丁语 largus，在表示「大」之前，它先表示慷慨、丰足。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get an adverb that says most of the whole is on one side.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly 得到的副词，意思是整体的大部分都落在一边。

normal.en: Largely because marks the main cause, not the only cause.
normal.cn: largely because 标出主要原因，而不是唯一原因。

normal.en: Largely ignored means ignored by most people, while largely unchanged means changed only a little.
normal.cn: largely ignored 指被大多数人忽视；largely unchanged 指只改变了一点点。

normal.en: The generous sense survives in older writing, where giving largely means giving freely.
normal.cn: 慷慨义留在较早的文字里，giving largely 就是慷慨地给予。

abstract.en: A word for an open hand became a word for the bigger share: abundance turns into proportion.
abstract.cn: 一个形容张开的手的词变成了「较大份额」的词：充裕转成了比例。

abstract.en: To say largely is to leave a small door open, because most is not all.
abstract.cn: 说 largely 就是留一扇小门，因为「大部分」并不等于全部。

abstract.en: The adverb measures a crowd as one body, not as a hundred separate opinions.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把人群当成一个整体来衡量，而不是一百个各自独立的意见。

examples.en: The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果被宣读时，人群大体上保持沉默。

examples.en: His early success was largely due to the people who taught him.
examples.cn: 他早期的成功很大程度上归功于教过他的人。

examples.en: The village is now largely deserted in winter.
examples.cn: 这个村子在冬天如今大都空着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉直了」——把大部分道理拉直说明白；谐音记住 largely 是主要地。

root: 由 large 加 -ly 构成；large 源自拉丁语 largus（充裕、慷慨），经古法语 large（宽、大）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the greater part of a whole; the word then measures degree, and an older sense of generous giving survives at the edge.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是整体中的较大部分；词义由此转为衡量程度，而「慷慨给予」的旧义留在边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with almost all the weight settled on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上几乎所有重量都压在一边。

branches.en: a mostly silent hall during an announcement
branches.cn: 宣布结果时大体安静的大厅

branches.en: a region that is mostly farmland
branches.cn: 大部分是农田的地区

branches.en: a success explained by one strong cause
branches.cn: 由一个强原因解释的成功

branches.en: a report left almost untouched
branches.cn: 几乎原封未动的报告

branches.en: an old lord giving freely to the poor
branches.cn: 老领主慷慨施舍穷人

intro.en: The word is an adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly, and the adjective itself comes from a Latin word for plenty.
intro.cn: 这个词是形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly，而形容词本身来自一个表示「丰足」的拉丁词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 最后的；上一个的；持续
definition_en: final in order, the most recent, or to continue for a time

senses.title: Final in order
senses.definition: Final in order
senses.definitionCN: 顺序上排在末尾
senses.example: She was the last to finish the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她是最后一个跑完比赛的。
senses.why: Last is a contraction of Old English latost, the superlative of late; it first meant furthest behind.
senses.whyCN: last 是古英语 latost 的缩约形式，即 late 的最高级；最初指落在最后的。

senses.title: The most recent
senses.definition: The most recent
senses.definitionCN: 最近过去的
senses.example: I saw him last week.
senses.exampleCN: 我上周见过他。
senses.why: Because the latest thing is also the one just before now, last came to mean the most recent.
senses.whyCN: 因为最近发生的事也就是此刻之前的那一件，last 就表示上一个的。

senses.title: To continue for a time
senses.definition: To continue for a time
senses.definitionCN: 延续一段时间
senses.example: The film lasts two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影持续两小时。
senses.why: The verb last is a separate Old English word, læstan, meaning to continue or endure.
senses.whyCN: 动词 last 是另一个古英语词 læstan，意为持续、忍受。

definition_zh: 晚的；迟到的；后期的；已故的；晚；迟
definition_en: happening after the usual time, far on in a period, no longer living, or after the expected moment
core_image: 散场后的走廊空无一人，墙上的钟已过整点
scene: 会议拖到很晚，走廊里只剩最后一盏灯。He arrived late and missed the opening speech.
sceneCN: 这里是「晚、迟」（第 4 个义项：副词，表示过了预期的时间）；句意为他到得很晚，错过了开场发言。可辨识画面：深夜的走廊、最后一盏灯、关上的会场门。

senses.title: Happening after the usual time
senses.definition: happening or arriving after the expected or usual time
senses.definitionCN: 在预期或平常时间之后发生或到达
senses.example: The train was late by twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 火车晚了二十分钟。
senses.why: The Germanic base meant slow or sluggish, so late first described something that comes after it should.
senses.whyCN: 日耳曼语词基的意思是迟缓、拖沓，所以 late 最初描述「该来而没按时来」的事物。

senses.title: No longer living
senses.definition: used before a name to say that the person has died recently
senses.definitionCN: 用在名字前，表示此人不久前已去世
senses.example: The late Mr Chen taught here for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 已故的陈先生在这里教了三十年书。
senses.why: Someone late is someone who has left, and the final departure of death gave the word this polite use.
senses.whyCN: late 可指「已经离开的」，而死亡是最后的离开，于是有了这层委婉说法。

senses.title: Far on in a period
senses.definition: near the end of a period of time, as in late autumn
senses.definitionCN: 接近一段时间的末尾，如深秋
senses.example: The library stays open until late in the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆开到晚上很晚。
senses.why: If something is slow to arrive, it naturally sits near the end of the stretch, so the word also marks the closing part of a period.
senses.whyCN: 事物来得慢，自然落在整段时间的尾端，所以这个词也用来标出一段时期的末尾。

senses.title: After the expected moment, as an adverb
senses.definition: after the expected or usual moment, used to describe the timing of an action
senses.definitionCN: 在预期或平常时刻之后，用来描述动作发生的时间
senses.example: She came home late after the concert.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会结束后她很晚才回家。
senses.why: The adverb simply applies the adjective's idea to the timing of an action rather than to the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 副词把形容词的比较用在动作发生的时间上，而不是用在事物本身。

intro.en: An Old English adjective of slowness grew into a word for lateness, the end of a period and a polite word for the dead.
intro.cn: 一个表示迟缓的古英语形容词，长成了表示迟到、时期末尾以及委婉指死者的词。

items.en: Læt meant slow, sluggish and tardy, describing people as well as times.
items.cn: læt 意为迟缓、拖沓、迟到，既形容人，也形容时间。

items.en: Middle English late kept the sense of tardy and added the sense of being far on in a period.
items.cn: 中古英语 late 保留「迟到」义，并加上「时期靠后」的意思。

items.en: The polite use for the dead appears late in the medieval period, as a softer way of saying departed.
items.cn: 用于死者的委婉说法出现于中古后期，是「已离去」的柔和说法。

items.en: The adverb use settles alongside the adjective, so late can describe when an action happens.
items.cn: 副词用法与形容词并行定型，于是 late 也能描述动作发生的时刻。

items.en: Modern English uses late for time, for the end of a period, and for the recently dead.
items.cn: 现代英语用 late 指时间晚、时期末尾，以及最近去世的人。

normalIntro.en: One Old English adjective of slowness carries every sense of this word, from a missed train to a quiet grave.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示迟缓的古英语形容词承载着这个词的每个义项，从错过的火车到安静的坟前。

normal.en: Old English læt meant slow, so late and the idea of tardiness grew from the same root.
normal.cn: 古英语 læt 意为迟缓，late 与「迟到」的观念同出一个根。

normal.en: Later and latest are the comparative and superlative, made by adding -er and -est.
normal.cn: later 与 latest 是比较级和最高级，由加 -er 与 -est 构成。

normal.en: Lately does not mean in a late way; it means recently, a different direction taken by the same word.
normal.cn: lately 不是「晚地」，而是「最近」，是同一个词走出的另一个方向。

normal.en: The late Mr Chen means the Mr Chen who has died, not the one who arrived late.
normal.cn: the late Mr Chen 指已去世的陈先生，不是迟到的陈先生。

normal.en: Late autumn is the closing part of the season, the same idea as a late hour of the day.
normal.cn: late autumn 是季节的末尾，与一天中「很晚的时刻」是同一个想法。

abstract.en: A word for slow turns into a word for the end of things, because what comes slowly arrives last.
abstract.cn: 表示迟缓的词变成了表示末尾的词，因为来得慢的东西最后才到。

abstract.en: Using late for the dead is politeness: it says departed rather than dead.
abstract.cn: 用 late 指死者是一种委婉：说的是「已离去」，而不是「死」。

abstract.en: Time words always carry judgement, so late can praise a ripe evening or blame a missed train.
abstract.cn: 时间词总带着评判，所以 late 既能形容成熟的夜晚，也能责怪错过的火车。

definition_zh: 更晚的；后来的；以后
definition_en: at a time after the present or after a stated moment; the comparative of late

senses.title: At a time after the present or a stated moment
senses.definition: happening or existing at a time after now or after a moment already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 发生在现在或已提到的某一时点之后
senses.example: The decision was postponed to a later date.
senses.exampleCN: 决定被推迟到更晚的日期。

senses.whyCN: later 就是 late 的比较级：时间线上有两个点，这个词指更靠后的那一个。

senses.title: Afterwards, at some future time
senses.definition: at a time in the future, especially after something else has happened
senses.definitionCN: 在将来的某个时间，尤指在另一件事之后
senses.example: We can discuss the details later.
senses.exampleCN: 细节我们可以以后再谈。

senses.whyCN: 形容词的比较义转为时间副词，于是 later 可以独立表示「后来」，不必再点出第二个时点。

intro.en: Later is the comparative of late, an Old English adjective for slow and tardy that shifted its centre to time.
intro.cn: later 是 late 的比较级；late 是古英语中表示「慢、迟」的形容词，后来重心转到时间上。

items.en: Læt meant slow, sluggish or tardy, describing a person or thing that moves behind time.
items.cn: læt 意为慢的、迟缓的、迟到的，描述落在时间后面的 人或物。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family that also gives German lass and the idea of letting go.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，同族还包括德语 lass 以及「放开」的概念。

items.en: The old comparative ending -ra produced lætra, the ancestor of later.
items.cn: 古老的比较级词尾 -ra 造出 lætra，即 later 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English later is fixed as the comparative of late and begins to work as an adverb.
items.cn: 中古英语中 later 固定为 late 的比较级，并开始作副词使用。

items.en: Modern English adds the fixed phrases later on and sooner or later.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 later on 与 sooner or later 这类固定短语。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same late family; the near-meaning group gathers words for a time that comes after.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 late 词族的各种形式；近义组收表示「之后」的时间词。

normal.en: Later is the comparative of late: late, later, latest.
normal.cn: later 是 late 的比较级：late、later、latest。

normal.en: Later on is a fixed phrase meaning 'afterwards'.
normal.cn: later on 是固定短语，意为「后来」。

normal.en: Sooner or later means at some time, whether soon or far off.
normal.cn: sooner or later 意为「迟早」。

normal.en: Latter is a cousin for 'the second of two', not for time alone.
normal.cn: latter 是表示「两者中后者」的近亲，不只用于时间。

normal.en: See you later is a farewell that names no exact time.
normal.cn: see you later 是不点明具体时间的告别语。

abstract.en: A comparative word can become a bare adverb, which shows how comparison turns into pure time.
abstract.cn: 一个比较级词可以变成独立的副词，说明比较如何转成纯粹的时间。

abstract.en: Later always needs an anchor: now, or an event just mentioned.
abstract.cn: later 总需要一个锚点：现在，或刚提到的一件事。

abstract.en: A word for slow became a word for late, and then for the future.
abstract.cn: 一个表示「慢」的词变成「迟」，再变成「将来」。
