examples.en: We can discuss the details later.
examples.cn: 细节我们可以以后再谈。

examples.en: Sooner or later, the truth will come out.
examples.cn: 真相迟早会显露出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累特」——拖到累得特晚，就是 later。

root: 古英语 læt（慢的、迟的）的比较级 lætra，词根属日耳曼语族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a second point further along the time line; it splits into the adjective 'later' and the adverb 'afterwards'.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是时间线上更靠后的第二个点；由此分成形容词「更晚的」与副词「后来」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page turned over, with a finger resting on the next page.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历翻过一页，手指停在后面那一页上。

branches.en: a meeting pushed from morning to afternoon
branches.cn: 从上午推到下午的会议

branches.en: a train that arrives after the timetable
branches.cn: 晚于点表到达的列车

branches.en: a promise to talk again another day
branches.cn: 改天再谈的承诺

branches.en: a letter read long after it was sent
branches.cn: 寄出很久之后才被读的信

branches.en: one step further along the same line
branches.cn: 同一条线上再往后一步

intro.en: The family is built on a short Old English adjective and its comparative endings.
intro.cn: 这个词族建立在很短的古英语形容词及其比较级词尾上。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 后者的；后半的；后期的
definition_en: referring to the second of two things already mentioned; belonging to the later part of a period; recent or modern in a formal phrase
core_image: 两张并排的卡片，手指落在右边那一张上
scene: 桌上摊着两份方案，他看了一会儿，把手指落在右边那份更薄的纸上。Of the two plans, the latter seemed cheaper and far simpler.
sceneCN: 这里是「后者的」（第 1 个义项：两个事物中的第二个）；句意是两份方案里，后者看起来更便宜也简单得多。图中可辨识物件：两份方案、桌面、手指。

collocations.zh: 在晚年；在后来的岁月里

derivatives.zh: 由 latter 加 -ly 构成，义为「在后期；最近」
由 latter 与 day 复合而成，义为「晚期的；现代的」

senses.title: The second of two things mentioned
senses.definition: the second of two people or things just mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚提到的两个人或事物中的第二个
senses.example: Of the two plans, the latter seemed cheaper and far simpler.
senses.exampleCN: 两份方案里，后者看起来更便宜也简单得多。
senses.why: The Old English comparative meant later, and when two things are listed in order the later one is the second, which is how the contrast with former arose.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的比较级意为「更晚的」，而两个事物按顺序列出时，较晚的那个就是第二个，与 former 的对举便由此形成。

senses.title: The later part of a period
senses.definition: belonging to the later part of a period or process
senses.definitionCN: 属于某段时期或过程的靠后部分
senses.example: The latter half of the book is far more exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书的后半部分要精彩得多。
senses.why: A period can be split into an earlier and a later part, so the old comparative of late naturally labels the second half.
senses.whyCN: 一段时间可以分成较早与较晚两部分，于是 late 的旧比较级自然被用来标记后半段。

senses.title: Recent or modern, in formal phrasing
senses.definition: recent or modern, especially in fixed phrases such as latter-day
senses.definitionCN: 近来的或现代的，尤见于 latter-day 这类固定说法
senses.example: He writes about latter-day heroes and their small daily battles.
senses.exampleCN: 他写的是现代英雄以及他们日常的小小战斗。
senses.why: What is later in time is also nearer to the present, so latter came to describe recent or modern things in formal usage.
senses.whyCN: 时间上更晚的也离现在更近，所以 latter 在正式用法里逐渐指近来或现代的事物。

intro.en: Latter is the old comparative of late, a Germanic word; English has kept it mainly for the second of two and for the later part of something.
intro.cn: latter 是 late 的旧比较级，而 late 是日耳曼语词；英语主要用它指两者中的后者和某事物的后半段。

items.en: Late goes back to a Germanic word for slow or sluggish, and its comparative had a form of its own.
items.cn: late 可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「慢、迟缓」的词，它的比较级另有形态。

items.en: Old English lætra was the comparative of læt and meant later or more slow.
items.cn: 古英语 lætra 是 læt 的比较级，意为更晚或更慢。

items.en: Middle English latter kept the comparative meaning and began to pair with former.
items.cn: 中古英语 latter 保留比较级含义，并开始与 former 对举。

items.en: Printing and formal prose fixed the pair the former and the latter for two things already named.
items.cn: 印刷术与正式散文把 the former 与 the latter 固定为指两个已提及事物的配对。

items.en: Modern English also uses latter for the later part of a period and for latter-day ideas.
items.cn: 现代英语还用 latter 指时期的后半段，以及 latter-day 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of late and compounds of latter; the near-meaning group collects words that order or oppose two things.
note.cn: 形近组收 late 的各种形式与 latter 的复合词；近义组收给两者排序或作对照的词。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after something else; the ordinary comparative of late.
entries.definitionCN: 在现在或某事之后的某个时间；late 的普通比较级。

entries.definition: Most recent in time; the superlative of late.
entries.definitionCN: 时间上最近的；late 的最高级。

entries.definition: Recently, or in the later part of a period.
entries.definitionCN: 最近，或在某段时期的后期。

entries.definition: Modern or recent, often used of a new version of an old type.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的或近来的，常指旧类型的新版本。

entries.definition: The first of two things mentioned; the direct partner of latter.
entries.definitionCN: 两个被提到的事物中的第一个；与 latter 直接配对。

entries.definition: Coming before the one now mentioned or current.
entries.definitionCN: 在现在提到或当前这个之前的。

entries.definition: Final in order, or most recent before the present.
entries.definitionCN: 顺序上的最后一个，或现在之前最近的。

entries.definition: Coming at the end of a series or process.
entries.definitionCN: 处在一串事物或过程末尾的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a frozen comparative, so its memory hooks are the pairing with former and the family of late forms around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个凝固的比较级，所以记忆抓手是与 former 的配对，以及周围 late 的各种形式。

normal.en: Latter and former are a fixed pair: former names the first of two, latter names the second.
normal.cn: latter 与 former 是固定配对：former 指两个中的第一个，latter 指第二个。

normal.en: Latter is not the same as later: later is about time, while latter is about position in a list of two.
normal.cn: latter 与 later 不同：later 谈时间，latter 谈两项列表中的位置。

normal.en: Latterly adds -ly to latter and means recently or in the later part of a period.
normal.cn: latterly 在 latter 后加 -ly，意为最近或某段时期的后期。

normal.en: Latter-day is a compound meaning modern, often suggesting a new version of something old.
normal.cn: latter-day 是表示「现代的」的复合词，常暗示旧事物的新版本。

normal.en: The word keeps an old comparative shape, which is why it has no comparative or superlative of its own.
normal.cn: 这个词保留了古老的比较级形态，所以它本身没有比较级或最高级。

abstract.en: Two things side by side create an order, and a language needs a short word for the second one.
abstract.cn: 两个事物并排就产生了顺序，而语言需要一个短词来指第二个。

abstract.en: Latter turns position into time: the second in a list is also the one that comes later.
abstract.cn: latter 把位置变成时间：列表中的第二个也是来得较晚的那一个。

abstract.en: A word that refuses to be compared reminds us that some grammatical forms are fossils of older stages.
abstract.cn: 一个拒绝再被比较的词提醒人：有些语法形式是更早阶段的化石。

examples.en: Of the two plans, the latter seemed cheaper and far simpler.
examples.cn: 两份方案里，后者看起来更便宜也简单得多。

examples.en: The latter half of the book is far more exciting.
examples.cn: 这本书的后半部分要精彩得多。

examples.en: She chose the latter option without a moment's doubt.
examples.cn: 她毫不犹豫地选了后一个选项。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「来特」——后来的那个才是「来特」；latter 指后者。

root: 古英语 lætra，是 læt（late）的比较级，属日耳曼语；与拉丁语无可靠同源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is second position in a pair; it extends to the later half of a period and to recent or modern things.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是成对事物中的第二位；由此延伸到一段时期的后半段，以及近来或现代的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two cards side by side, with a finger resting on the right-hand one.
core.cn: 核心意象：两张并排的卡片，手指落在右边那一张上。

branches.en: two names on a list, with the finger on the second
branches.cn: 名单上两个名字，手指停在第二个

branches.en: a formal sentence naming the former and the latter
branches.cn: 一句话里前者与后者并排出现

branches.en: a clock moving through the second half of the year
branches.cn: 时钟走过一年的后半段

branches.en: a modern hero inside an old-fashioned tale
branches.cn: 旧式故事里的现代英雄

branches.en: a choice settled by the later of two offers
branches.cn: 在两份报价中由较晚到来的那一份决定

intro.en: A frozen comparative of late is surrounded by the ordinary comparative, superlative and adverb of late, plus one compound with day.
intro.cn: late 的凝固比较级周围，是 late 的普通比较级、最高级、副词，以及一个与 day 组成的复合词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: recently or in the later part

definition_zh: 笑；发笑；笑声；嘲笑
definition_en: to make the sounds and movements that show you are amused, or the sound so made
core_image: 一桌人听到笑话，筷子停在半空，笑声先响起来
scene: 饭桌上有人讲了个笨笑话，满桌人先愣了一秒。Then everyone began to laugh at the same moment.
sceneCN: 这里是「笑、发笑」（第 1 个义项：因为觉得有趣而发出笑声）；句意为随后所有人同时笑了起来。可辨识画面：饭桌、停住的筷子、一张张笑脸。

derivatives.zh: 由 laugh 加名词后缀 -ter 构成，义为「笑；笑声」
由 laugh 加 -able（可……的）构成，义为「可笑的」
由 laughing 加 -ly 构成，义为「笑着地」
由 laughing 与 stock 复合，义为「笑柄」

senses.title: To make the sounds of being amused
senses.definition: to make the sounds and face movements that show you are amused
senses.definitionCN: 发出表示觉得好笑的声音与表情
senses.example: The children laughed at the puppet show.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们看着木偶戏笑了起来。
senses.why: The word is probably imitative: the sound of laughing became the name of laughing, so the mouth noise is the whole origin.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能是拟声的：笑的声音变成了「笑」的名字，嘴里的声响就是它的全部来源。

senses.title: The sound of laughing
senses.definition: the sound made when someone laughs
senses.definitionCN: 人发笑时发出的声音
senses.example: Her laugh was loud enough to fill the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑声大得能填满整个大厅。
senses.why: Once the noise has a name, the noise itself can be counted, so the verb's sound becomes a noun you can hear once.
senses.whyCN: 声音有了名字也就可以计数，于是动词的声响变成可以「听到一次」的名词。

senses.title: To make fun of someone
senses.definition: to treat someone as silly, often with unkind laughter
senses.definitionCN: 把某人当作可笑的人，常带不友善的笑
senses.example: They laughed at his old coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们嘲笑他那件旧外套。
senses.why: Laughing together excludes someone, and that social edge turned the plain verb into a word for mockery.
senses.whyCN: 一起笑会把某人排除在外，这层社交锋芒让普通动词有了讥笑的意思。

senses.title: An amusing person or occasion
senses.definition: a person or event that makes people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 让人发笑的人或场合
senses.example: The party was a good laugh.
senses.exampleCN: 那场聚会挺好玩。
senses.why: If laughing is the effect, then whatever causes it can borrow the name, which is how the noun becomes a label for fun.
senses.whyCN: 既然笑是结果，造成笑的东西也能借用这个名字，名词于是成了「好玩」的标签。

intro.en: The word probably copies the sound of laughing, and that imitative shape has survived since Old English.
intro.cn: 这个词很可能模仿笑的声音，这种拟声的形态从古英语一直留存至今。

items.en: A Germanic base for laughing, probably imitative of the sound, is the likely origin.
items.cn: 一般认为源自日耳曼语中表示笑的词基，很可能是对笑声的模仿。

items.en: Old English hlæhhan meant to laugh, with forms that kept the h and the rough breath.
items.cn: 古英语 hlæhhan 意为笑，词形保留了 h 与粗糙的送气。

items.en: Middle English laughen softened the opening sound and lost the old ending.
items.cn: 中古英语 laughen 软化了词首音，并丢掉了旧词尾。

items.en: The modern spelling laugh settles while the pronunciation keeps the f sound of the old ending.
items.cn: 现代拼写 laugh 定型，而读音仍保留旧词尾的 f 音。

items.en: Modern English uses laugh for the act, the sound, mockery and a good time.
items.cn: 现代英语用 laugh 指发笑的动作、笑声、取笑，也指开心的场合。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words made from the same laughing stem; the near-meaning group collects other kinds of smiling and laughing.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一个「笑」词干构成的词；近义组收其他表示微笑与发笑的词。

entries.definition: The noun for laughing as a whole, not counting one laugh.
entries.definitionCN: 表示笑声整体的名词，不数单次的笑。

entries.definition: So silly that it makes people laugh.
entries.definitionCN: 荒唐得让人发笑的。

entries.definition: Doing something with laughter, or in a light way.
entries.definitionCN: 笑着做某事，或以轻描淡写的方式。

entries.definition: A person who is laughed at by everyone.
entries.definitionCN: 被众人取笑的人。

entries.definition: To lift the corners of the mouth in pleasure, without sound.
entries.definitionCN: 愉快地嘴角上扬，不出声。

entries.definition: To laugh in a light, silly way.
entries.definitionCN: 轻声傻笑。

entries.definition: To laugh quietly to yourself.
entries.definitionCN: 自顾自地低声笑。

entries.definition: To smile widely with the teeth showing.
entries.definitionCN: 露齿咧嘴笑。

normalIntro.en: A probably imitative Germanic verb, three English endings and one compound keep this word going.
normalIntro.cn: 一个很可能是拟声的日耳曼动词、三个英语词尾与一个复合词，让这个词延续下来。

normal.en: Laugh is probably imitative, so the sound of laughing is older than the word's spelling.
normal.cn: laugh 很可能是拟声的，笑的声音比这个词的拼写更古老。

normal.en: Old English hlæhhan had a rough h at the start, while Modern English laugh keeps only the f at the end.
normal.cn: 古英语 hlæhhan 开头有粗糙的 h 音，而现代英语 laugh 只在词尾留下 f 音。

normal.en: Laughter is the mass noun, so you say much laughter but a loud laugh.
normal.cn: laughter 是表示整体的名词，所以说 much laughter，而 a loud laugh 指一声笑。

normal.en: Laugh at means to mock, while laugh with means to share the joke.
normal.cn: laugh at 意为嘲笑，laugh with 意为与人一起笑。

normal.en: Laughing stock is the person every joke is aimed at.
normal.cn: laughing stock 是每个玩笑都对准的那个人。

abstract.en: English spells laugh oddly because it froze a sound that no longer matches the letters.
abstract.cn: 英语把 laugh 拼得古怪，因为它冻结了一个与字母已对不上的读音。

abstract.en: A shared laugh builds a group while a mocking laugh draws its border, so one sound does both.
abstract.cn: 共同的笑建立群体，讥笑则画出边界，同一种声音同时做两件事。

abstract.en: To laugh off a problem is to shrink it with sound instead of solving it.
abstract.cn: laugh off 一个问题，是用笑声把它缩小，而不是解决它。

examples.en: The children laughed at the puppet show.
examples.cn: 孩子们看着木偶戏笑了起来。

examples.en: Her laugh was loud enough to fill the hall.
examples.cn: 她的笑声大得能填满整个大厅。

examples.en: We had a good laugh over the photo.
examples.cn: 看着那张照片，我们笑了好一阵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉夫」——讲笑话把人逗得直拍手，笑声能拉来一群人；记住 laugh 是笑。

root: 一般认为来自日耳曼语表示笑的词基，可能模仿笑声；古英语写作 hlæhhan。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the sound of amusement; the senses then divide into the act, the sound itself, mockery and a fun occasion.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是觉得有趣时发出的声响；义项由此分为动作、声音本身、取笑，以及好玩的场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: chopsticks paused in mid-air while laughter fills a dining room.
core.cn: 核心意象：筷子停在半空，笑声充满整间饭厅。

branches.en: a table of people breaking into the same sound
branches.cn: 一桌人同时爆出同一种声音

branches.en: a single laugh ringing through a hall
branches.cn: 一声笑在大厅里回响

branches.en: a group turning a joke against one person
branches.cn: 一群人把玩笑对准一个人

branches.en: a photo passed around and laughed over
branches.cn: 传着看、被笑个不停的照片

branches.en: a child's face open in a wide laugh
branches.cn: 孩子张大嘴笑的脸

intro.en: A Germanic verb that probably copies the sound, plus three modern endings that build nouns and adjectives from it.
intro.cn: 一个很可能是模仿笑声的日耳曼动词，加上三个由此造出名词与形容词的现代词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic and probably imitative; Latin ridere for laughing is a different root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语，很可能是拟声的；拉丁语表示笑的 ridere 是另一个词根。

items.meaning: to make the sound of amusement
items.meaningCN: 发出表示觉得有趣的声音

items.meaning: laughing plus stock, a target of jokes
items.meaningCN: laughing 与 stock 复合，被取笑的目标

definition_zh: 发射；发起；推出；（船）下水；发射活动；（产品的）发布
definition_en: to send a ship, rocket or product into motion or into the market, and the act of starting something new
core_image: 船坞闸门打开，新船顺着滑道冲向水面
scene: 码头上挤满了来看新船下水的人。The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 launch 指「使船下水」（第 1 个义项）；句意为船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。图中可辨识物件：船坞闸门、滑道、围观的人群。

collocations.phrase: the launch of a new service

derivatives.zh: 由 launch 加 -er 构成，指发射装置或发射者
由 launch 与 pad 复合，指发射台、起飞平台
由 re- 加 launch 构成，指重新推出、再次发起

senses.title: To send a newly built ship into the water
senses.definition: to move a newly built boat from the slipway into the water for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 把新造的船第一次从滑道送入水中
senses.example: The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。
senses.why: The word began as a lance thrown forward, so the first maritime use pictured a hull driven down a slipway like a weapon released.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指向前掷出的长矛，因此最早的船舶用法把船体沿滑道冲下，想象成一件被放出的武器。

senses.title: To start an activity, company or product
senses.definition: to begin something new such as a business, a campaign or a product, and make it public
senses.definitionCN: 开始并公开推出企业、运动或产品等新事物
senses.example: The company will launch its new phone next month.
senses.exampleCN: 公司下个月将推出新手机。
senses.why: Starting a venture is like setting a ship afloat: both release something built in private into the open, where it must stay afloat on its own.
senses.whyCN: 开创一项事业就像让船下水：两者都把在内部造好的东西放出去，此后它必须自己浮在水面上。

senses.title: To send a rocket or spacecraft into the air
senses.definition: to send a rocket, missile or spacecraft up into the sky or into space
senses.definitionCN: 把火箭、导弹或航天器送上天空或太空
senses.example: They launched the satellite from a desert site.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在沙漠场地发射了那颗卫星。
senses.why: A rocket is thrown upward the way a lance was thrown, and the old image of a forceful release fits the modern machine exactly.
senses.whyCN: 火箭被向上抛出，正如长矛被掷出，那个「用力放出」的旧画面恰好贴合现代机器。

senses.title: The act of launching something
senses.definition: the event or act of starting, releasing or putting something into service, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 启动、放出或让某物投入使用的活动，作名词
senses.example: The launch of the new service was covered by every paper.
senses.exampleCN: 新服务的发布被各家报纸报道。
senses.why: English often turns a forceful verb into a noun, so the moment of release becomes a public event with guests and speeches.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把有力的动词变成名词，于是「放出的那一刻」成了有来宾和致辞的公开活动。

intro.en: Launch goes back to a Latin word for a spear, and the idea of hurling something forward runs through all of its senses.
intro.cn: launch 可追到拉丁语中表示长矛的词，而「把东西向前掷出」这个意思贯穿它的所有义项。

items.en: Lancea meant a light spear, the weapon carried by a lancer.
items.cn: lancea 指轻矛，是长矛手使用的武器。

items.en: Lanceare meant to wield a lance, and in French the sense widened to throwing or driving something forward.
items.cn: lanceare 意为挥动长矛，在法语中词义扩大到把东西向前投出或推动。

items.en: Old French lanchier meant to hurl a spear or to set a boat afloat, and English borrowed both ideas.
items.cn: 古法语 lanchier 意为投掷矛枪或让船下水，英语把这两种意思都借了过来。

items.en: Middle English launch kept the movement sense: to let something go forward, whether a boat, a weapon or a shout.
items.cn: 中古英语 launch 保留「向前放出」的意思：无论是船、武器还是一声喊。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from ships to rockets and businesses, so launch now starts almost anything.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从船扩展到火箭与企业，于是 launch 几乎能「启动」任何东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the lance family and its built forms; the near-meaning group collects verbs for beginning or releasing something.
note.cn: 形近组收 lance 一词族及其构成形式；近义组收表示开始或放出的动词。

entries.definition: A device or person that sends something into the air.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物送上天空的装置或人。

entries.definition: The platform from which a rocket leaves the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 火箭升空所依托的平台。

entries.definition: A long spear, the weapon behind the word.
entries.definitionCN: 长矛，是这个词背后的武器。

entries.definition: To begin doing or making something.
entries.definitionCN: 开始做或开始制造某物。

entries.definition: To set a process or plan going.
entries.definitionCN: 启动一个过程或计划。

entries.definition: To let something go out or become available.
entries.definitionCN: 放出某物或使其可获取。

entries.definition: To shoot a weapon or set off a rocket.
entries.definitionCN: 射击武器或点火发射火箭。

normalIntro.en: A spear thrown forward is the oldest picture inside this word, and every later sense repeats the same release.
normalIntro.cn: 一支向前掷出的长矛是这个词里最古老的画面，此后每个义项都在重复同一次「放出」。

normal.en: Latin lancea is a spear, and lanceare means to use one, which is the physical core of launch.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lancea 是长矛，lanceare 是使用长矛，这就是 launch 的物理核心。

normal.en: A ship is launched down a slipway, driven forward like a thrown weapon.
normal.cn: 船沿滑道下水，像被掷出的武器一样被推向前方。

normal.en: A product launch borrows the same gesture: something built inside is pushed out into the market.
normal.cn: 产品发布借用同一个动作：在内部造好的东西被推向市场。

normal.en: A rocket launch repeats the old throw upward, with fire instead of muscle.
normal.cn: 火箭发射重复了古老的向上投掷，只是用火代替了肌肉。

normal.en: Launcher and launchpad name the tool and the place that make the release possible.
normal.cn: launcher 与 launchpad 指让这次「放出」得以发生的工具和地点。

abstract.en: One verb covers ships, rockets and businesses because all three must leave the place where they were built.
abstract.cn: 一个动词涵盖船、火箭与企业，因为三者都必须离开自己被造出来的地方。

abstract.en: A launch is a public moment because release is risky: once it is out, it must float without help.
abstract.cn: 发布是公开的时刻，因为放出有风险：一旦出去，它必须自己浮着。

abstract.en: The lance became a satellite, but the gesture is still a throw.
abstract.cn: 长矛变成了卫星，可那个动作仍然是一次投掷。

examples.en: The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
examples.cn: 船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。

examples.en: The company will launch its new phone next month.
examples.cn: 公司下个月将推出新手机。

examples.en: They launched the satellite from a desert site.
examples.cn: 他们在沙漠场地发射了那颗卫星。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「浪起」——浪头起来了，船就下水、火箭就升空；谐音记住 launch 是发射、发起。

root: 源自拉丁语 lancea（长矛）与 lanceare（挥矛），经古法语 lanchier（投矛、使船下水）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is something thrown forward; it becomes a ship sliding into water, a rocket rising, and a product sent into the market.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是把东西向前掷出；它化为滑入水中的船、升空的火箭，以及推向市场的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dock gates open and a new hull slides down the slipway into the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：船坞闸门打开，新船体沿滑道冲入水中。

branches.en: a hull sliding down greased timbers
branches.cn: 船体沿涂油的木滑道下滑

branches.en: a crowd watching a ferry enter the water
branches.cn: 人群看着渡轮入水

branches.en: a phone shown on a stage for the first time
branches.cn: 手机第一次在台上亮相

branches.en: a rocket clearing the tower
branches.cn: 火箭飞离发射塔

branches.en: newspapers reporting a service launch
branches.cn: 报纸报道一项服务的发布

intro.en: A Latin spear and its verb pass through French into English, and English adds -er and a compound to name the tools of release.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「矛」及其动词经法语进入英语，英语又加 -er 和复合成分来命名放出的工具。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 法律（总称）；一条法律；定律；规则；执法机构；法学
definition_en: a rule that a community accepts as binding, or the whole system of such rules, or a regular pattern in nature
core_image: 石柱上刻着一排条文，旁边站着执法的人，远处实验室的黑板上写着另一条「定律」
scene: 公告栏上钉着新条文，摊主们围着读，谁也没先开口。The new law reaches every stall in the market.
sceneCN: 这里 law 指正式颁行的一条法律（第 2 个义项：一部法律）；句意为这条新法律管到市场上的每一个摊位。

pos.zh: （口语，用定冠词）执法机构；警方

derivatives.zh: 合法的（law + -ful「充满」，由法律转指符合其要求）
无法无天的（law + -less「无」，由法律转指其缺失）
律师（law + -yer「从事者」，由法律转指以此为业的人）
亡命之徒；宣布非法（out「在外」+ law，由法律转指被逐出法外）

senses.title: The system of rules
senses.definition: the whole body of binding rules of a community, seen as one system
senses.definitionCN: 某一社群全部有约束力的规则，被视为一个体系
senses.example: Law is slow, but it remembers.
senses.exampleCN: 法律很慢，但它记得住。
senses.why: the mass-noun use is the oldest general sense: law as an institution rather than a list of items.
senses.whyCN: 不可数用法是最古老的泛指义：法作为制度，而非条目清单。

senses.title: A single statute
senses.definition: one enacted rule with a number, a date and an issuing body
senses.definitionCN: 带编号、日期与颁行机关的单条规则
senses.example: The new law reaches every stall in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新法律管到市场上的每一个摊位。
senses.why: English made law countable so that individual acts could be cited and dated.
senses.whyCN: 英语让 law 可数，以便单条法令可被引用与记年。

senses.title: A regularity of nature
senses.definition: a statement that a natural process always behaves in a specified way
senses.definitionCN: 断言某一自然过程总以特定方式进行的陈述
senses.example: The law holds far from the laboratory as well.
senses.exampleCN: 这条定律在实验室之外也成立。
senses.why: the seventeenth century extended the word from decrees to regularities, since both are rules that cannot be broken.
senses.whyCN: 17 世纪把这个词从法令扩展到规律，因为两者都是不可违反的规则。

senses.title: A rule of a game or body
senses.titleCN: 比赛或机构内部的规则
senses.definition: an agreed rule governing play, a society or an institution
senses.definitionCN: 约定管辖比赛、社团或机构的规则
senses.example: The law of the club is older than the clubhouse.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部的规则比会所还老。
senses.why: any self-governing body reproduces the statute model, so the word follows the rule wherever it binds.
senses.whyCN: 任何自治团体都会复制法令的模式，于是这个词跟着规则走到哪里绑到哪里。

senses.title: The police, in speech
senses.definition: the police or the enforcement arm, used with the definite article
senses.definitionCN: 警察或执法部门，惯用定冠词
senses.example: The law arrived twenty minutes after the alarm.
senses.exampleCN: 警笛响过二十分钟后警察就到了。
senses.why: metonymy names the enforcers by the thing they enforce, an old colloquial habit.
senses.whyCN: 转喻用所执行之物来称呼执行者，是古老的口语习惯。

senses.title: The study and profession
senses.definition: the academic discipline of law and the profession that practises it
senses.definitionCN: 研究法律的学科以及以此执业的行业
senses.example: She read law before joining the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 她入部之前读的是法律。
senses.why: a body of rules large enough to need specialists becomes a discipline and a career.
senses.whyCN: 规则多到需要专家时，便成为一门学科与一种职业。

senses.title: A governing principle
senses.definition: a principle that explains how a domain works, as in the law of supply and demand
senses.definitionCN: 解释某一领域如何运作的原理，如供需法则
senses.example: The law of supply and demand explains the queue, not the price.
senses.exampleCN: 供需法则解释的是排队，不是价格。
senses.why: economics borrowed the prestige of natural law to describe tendencies that hold on average.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借来自然法的威望，用来描述平均成立的趋势。

senses.title: An inescapable rule
senses.definition: a rule presented as unavoidable, as in the law of the jungle
senses.definitionCN: 被说成不可避免的规则，如丛林法则
senses.example: The law of the jungle returned when the patrols stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 巡逻一停，丛林法则就回来了。
senses.why: the figurative use keeps the binding force and drops the institution, leaving only inevitability.
senses.whyCN: 比喻用法保留了约束力而丢掉机构，只剩不可避免。

intro.en: Law comes from Old English lagu, itself borrowed from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', from leggja 'to lay'. It has no Latin source, unlike legal and legislation. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: law 来自古英语 lagu，而 lagu 借自古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」，出自 leggja「放置」。与 legal、legislation 不同，它没有拉丁来源。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lag meant 'something laid down, a layer, a fixed order', from the verb leggja 'to lay'. The image is a rule placed down where people can see it.
items.cn: lag 意为「被放下之物、层次、既定秩序」，出自动词 leggja「放置」。意象是被放在人们看得见之处的规则。

items.en: Old English borrowed lagu from Norse during the Viking period; the native word for divine law was ǣ, which later dropped out.
items.cn: 古英语在维京时期从诺斯语借入 lagu；本土表示神法的词是 ǣ，后来消失。

items.en: Lagu settled into Middle English as lawe, taking over the general sense of binding custom and statute.
items.cn: lagu 进入中古英语作 lawe，接管了有约束力的习俗与法令这一泛义。

items.en: From the seventeenth century law was applied to regularities of nature, so that a falling apple and a statute shared one word.
items.cn: 17 世纪起 law 被用于自然规律，于是落下的苹果与一条法令共用同一个词。

items.en: Legal, legitimate and legislation descend from Latin lex, not from lagu; the resemblance is in meaning only, and the two families are unrelated at the root.
items.cn: legal、legitimate、legislation 上溯拉丁 lex，而非 lagu；相似只在意义上，两个词族在词根上并无关系。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Norse origin of lag is not established, and the relation sometimes proposed between lag and the English verb lay is plausible but not demonstrated as a direct derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：lag 在诺斯语之前的来源未得到证明；有人提出 lag 与英语动词 lay 的关系，看似合理，却未被证明为直接派生。

note.en: Group one gathers words that look related to law but come from Latin lex; group two holds near neighbours in the legal field.
note.cn: 第一组是看着与 law 有关、实际来自拉丁 lex 的词；第二组是法律领域的近义词。

entries.definition: From Latin legalis, built on lex; it means permitted by law, not the law itself, and is unrelated at the root to law.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 legalis，由 lex 构成；意为法律允许的，而非法律本身，与 law 在词根上无关。

entries.definition: The making of laws, from lex and latus; it names the process, not the Norse-rooted body of rules.
entries.definitionCN: 制定法律，来自 lex 与 latus；指过程，而非那个诺斯语词根的规则总体。

entries.definition: law plus -ful: conforming to the rules, an adjective built on the native noun.
entries.definitionCN: law 加 -ful：符合规则的，是本族名词派生的形容词。

entries.definition: Out 'outside' plus law: one placed outside the law's protection, so the root is kept and reversed.
entries.definitionCN: out「在外」加 law：被置于法律保护之外的人，词根保留而意义反转。

entries.definition: A formal written law passed by a legislature; law is the wider word that also covers custom and case law.
entries.definitionCN: 立法机关通过的正式成文法；law 是更宽的说法，也涵盖习惯法与判例法。

entries.definition: A regulation of an activity or a game; law implies a community's binding authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 某项活动或比赛的规章；law 暗含社群约束性权威在其背后。

entries.definition: A rule issued by an agency under a statute; it is law in a derived, technical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 机关依法令发布的规则；在派生、技术的意义上也是法。

entries.definition: A general truth that explains workings; it matches the scientific sense of law without any authority behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 解释运作的一般真理；对应 law 的科学义，背后却没有权威。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old Norse lag 'something laid down': a rule is a thing placed where all can see it.
normal.cn: 古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」：规则就是放在人人看得见之处的东西。

normal.en: The family runs lawful, lawless, lawyer, outlaw, by-law.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lawful、lawless、lawyer、outlaw、by-law。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: break the law, by law, the rule of law, a law of nature.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分出义项：违法、依法、法治、自然定律。

normal.en: Two senses share one word: the statute in the book and the regularity on the blackboard.
normal.cn: 两个义项共用一个词：书里的法令与黑板上的规律。

normal.en: Keep legal apart: it comes from Latin lex, so its resemblance to law is meaning, not blood.
normal.cn: 把 legal 分开放：它来自拉丁 lex，与 law 的相似是意义上的，不是血缘上的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone with lines cut into it, standing where everyone walks past.
abstract.cn: 想象一块刻着横线的石头，立在人人都经过的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a rule that keeps working after the person who wrote it is gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一条规则，写它的人不在了，它还在运作。

abstract.en: Picture two blackboards, one with a statute, one with an equation, both called law.
abstract.cn: 想象两块黑板，一块写着法令，一块写着方程，都叫 law。

examples.en: The law requires the seller to name the origin of the goods.
examples.cn: 法律要求卖方标明货物的产地。

examples.en: By law, the minutes must be public within a month.
examples.cn: 依法，会议记录必须在一个月内公开。

examples.en: The law of demand fails when buyers cannot compare prices.
examples.cn: 当买方无法比较价格时，需求法则就失效。

dict_mnemonic.text: law＝「放下的东西」：一条条放在那里、谁都得照着走；记「书里有条文，黑板上有定律」。

root: 古英语 lagu ← 古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」← leggja「放置」；lag 在诺斯语之前的来源不确定，与英语 lay 的关系仅为合理推测。与拉丁 lex 词族（legal、legislation）无词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses spread from one laid-down rule: the system, a single act, a regularity of nature, a game rule, the police, the profession, an economic principle, and an unavoidable rule of the jungle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一条被放下的规则散开：体系、单条法令、自然规律、比赛规则、警方、法律职业、经济原理，以及丛林里的必然规矩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rule laid down in public, heavy enough that people arrange their days around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条当众放下的规则，重到人们要围着它安排日子。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND UNIT: the whole body of rules, then one dated item inside it.
branches.cn: 体系与单位：规则总体，以及其中一条记年的条目。

branches.en: RULES WITHOUT A LAWGIVER: nature and the market exhibit regularities that cannot be disobeyed.
branches.cn: 没有立法者的规则：自然与市场呈现不可违背的规律。

branches.en: SMALL SCALES OF BINDING: a club's rulebook, and the jungle's unavoidable order.
branches.cn: 约束的小尺度：俱乐部的规则手册，以及丛林的必然秩序。

branches.en: THE ENFORCERS: the police named by what they enforce.
branches.cn: 执行者：用所执行之物来称呼警察。

branches.en: THE DISCIPLINE: a body of rules large enough to become a career.
branches.cn: 学科：规则多到足以成为一种职业。

intro.en: Law is a Norse loanword, so its family is built with English suffixes rather than Latin ones, unlike legal and legislation.
intro.cn: law 是诺斯语借词，因此其词族由英语后缀而非拉丁后缀构成，这一点与 legal、legislation 不同。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin entry here: the Latin lex family supplies legal and legislation but is not related to law at the root.
latinIntro.cn: 此处没有拉丁条目：拉丁 lex 词族给出 legal 与 legislation，但与 law 在词根上无关。

items.meaning: a binding rule; the body of such rules
items.meaningCN: 有约束力的规则；此类规则的总体
items.example: The law was read from the steps.
The search was lawful but rude.
The port grew lawless after the garrison left.
items.exampleCN: 驻军撤走后港口变得无法无天。

items.example: Her lawyer read the clause twice.
items.exampleCN: 她的律师把条款读了两遍。

items.meaning: one put outside the law; to ban
items.meaningCN: 被置于法外者；宣布非法
items.example: The practice was outlawed in the last session.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法在上个会期被宣布非法。

items.example: The by-law limits noise after ten.
items.exampleCN: 该细则限制十点后的噪音。

items.example: The legality of the order was disputed.
items.exampleCN: 这道命令的合法性受到质疑。

definition_zh: 律师；法律工作者
definition_en: a person who practises law, advising clients or pleading cases
core_image: 一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗堆在办公桌上，桌边的人正把其中一条条款圈出来给来访者看
scene: 当事人带着一份读不懂的租约走进办公室，想知道哪几条会让自己吃亏。The lawyer marked three clauses that could cost the tenant money.
sceneCN: 这里 lawyer 指以法律为业的执业者（第 1 个义项：从事法律工作的专业人员）；句意：这位律师标出了三条可能让租客多花钱的条款。图中可辨识物件：租约、彩色标签、红笔圈痕、办公桌。

pos.zh: 律师（泛指以法律为业者，可提供咨询或代理诉讼）

collocations.zh: 好抬杠的水手；爱抠规则的人

derivatives.zh: 律师式的；像律师那样措辞的
律师工作；办案实务
好争辩的水手；爱抠规则者
法律；法规

senses.title: A person who practises law
senses.definition: someone whose profession is law, whether advising or representing
senses.definitionCN: 以法律为职业的人，提供咨询或代理皆可
senses.example: The lawyer marked three clauses that could cost the tenant money.
senses.exampleCN: 律师标出了三条可能让租客多花钱的条款。
senses.why: The word is built from law plus an agent ending, so it names the profession by its subject matter rather than by a court role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「法律」加施事后缀构成，所以它按业务内容命名职业，而不是按法庭角色命名。

senses.title: An adviser working outside court
senses.definition: a legal adviser whose work is done in an office rather than in court
senses.definitionCN: 主要在办公室而非法庭上工作的法律顾问
senses.example: Our lawyer reviewed the insurance policy line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的律师逐行审阅了保险条款。
senses.why: Most legal work is paperwork and advice, so the everyday word usually points to the desk rather than to the dock.
senses.whyCN: 多数法律工作是文书与咨询，所以这个日常词通常指向办公桌，而不是法庭上的席位。

senses.title: An advocate who speaks in court
senses.definition: a legal practitioner who argues a case before a judge
senses.definitionCN: 在法官面前为案件辩论的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer spoke for forty minutes without looking at her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师讲了四十分钟，全程没看笔记。
senses.why: The same noun serves the courtroom because advocacy is the part of the profession the public sees and remembers.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也用于法庭，因为辩护是公众看得见、记得住的那部分工作。

senses.title: The profession as a group
senses.definition: lawyers considered collectively, often in commentary or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 被整体看待的律师，常用于评论或批评
senses.example: The lawyers for both sides met privately before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，双方的律师私下见了面。
senses.why: A countable noun used in the plural can stand for a whole trade, which is why the word appears in sentences about the profession as a force.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用复数时可以代表整个行业，所以这个词会出现在把律师界当作一股力量的句子里。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a practitioner who works in a particular field of law
senses.definitionCN: 在某一法律领域执业的律师
senses.example: They consulted a patent lawyer before filing the design.
senses.exampleCN: 申请外观设计前，他们咨询了专利律师。
senses.why: Modern law divides into fields, and the word attaches to the field as a modifier, turning the general noun into a specialism.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律分成许多领域，这个词作为修饰成分附着在领域上，就把通称变成了专业分工。

senses.title: The person who drafts the papers
senses.definition: the practitioner who prepares contracts, deeds and other documents
senses.definitionCN: 准备合同、契据等文书的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer drafted the deed so that either heir could sell.
senses.exampleCN: 律师起草的契据让两位继承人都能出售。
senses.why: Drafting is invisible in court but decisive in outcome, so the word also covers the quiet work behind a signature.
senses.whyCN: 起草在法庭上看不见，却决定结果，所以这个词也覆盖签名背后那份安静的工作。

senses.title: A sea lawyer
senses.titleCN: 好抬杠的水手；爱抠规则的人
senses.definition: an argumentative sailor, or anyone who quibbles about rules without authority
senses.definitionCN: 爱争辩的水手，或任何没有职权却抠规则字眼的人
senses.example: The cook was a sea lawyer who could quote every regulation but never follow one.
senses.exampleCN: 那个厨子是个爱抬杠的水手，条条规则都能背，却一条也不照做。
senses.why: Sailors with time on their hands argued about regulations, and the fixed phrase transferred that habit to land as a mild insult.
senses.whyCN: 水手闲来无事就争论规章，这个固定说法把这种习气带上岸，成了轻度的讥称。

senses.title: A clever arguer on technicalities
senses.definition: a person who argues by exploiting fine points rather than by merit
senses.definitionCN: 靠抠细枝末节而非讲道理取胜的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a lawyer to win that argument, only patient.
senses.exampleCN: 赢那场争论不必是律师，只需要有耐心。
senses.why: Because the trade is associated with precise wording, the noun can describe anyone who fights with clauses instead of facts.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个行业与精确措辞联系在一起，这个名词便能描述任何用条款而非事实来争论的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is an English compound of law and an agent ending. Law comes from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', while the ending is a variant of -ier from Old French, ultimately Latin -arius.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语用 law 加施事后缀构成的复合词。law 来自古诺斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，词尾则是古法语 -ier 的变体，最终上溯拉丁 -arius。

items.en: Lag meant something laid down, a layer or a fixed order; its plural log named customary law in the Norse-speaking world.
items.cn: lag 意为被放下的东西、一层或既定秩序；其复数 lǫg 在诺斯语世界指习惯法。

items.en: English borrowed lagu for law, covering both the body of rules and the custom of a district, a word that displaced the older native term.
items.cn: 英语借入 lagu 表示法律，既指整套规则，也指一地的习惯，并取代了更早的本族词。

items.en: The Latin agent suffix -arius, through Old French -ier, formed words for people concerned with a thing, and it is the source of the ending here.
items.cn: 拉丁施事后缀 -arius 经古法语 -ier，构成「与某物打交道的人」，这里这个词尾正源于此。

items.en: Middle English had lawier beside lawyer; the spelling with y won out, and the word settled on the profession as a whole.
items.cn: 中古英语里 lawier 与 lawyer 并存，带 y 的拼法最终胜出，这个词也固定指整个职业。

items.en: Modern English uses lawyer as the neutral everyday term, while attorney carries American formality and counsel carries courtroom colour.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lawyer 当作中性日常说法，attorney 带美国式的正式感，counsel 则带法庭色彩。

note.en: Group one separates the base word and the derived family from two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the plain word against the formal and regional titles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词与派生词族，同两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把日常通称与正式称谓、地区称谓作对照。

entries.definition: The rules themselves; lawyer is the person whose trade is those rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则本身；lawyer 是以这些规则为业的人。

entries.definition: Resembling a lawyer or the manner of legal argument, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 像律师的、像法律辩论腔调的，不是指人。

entries.definition: The practice or craft of being a lawyer, viewed as work rather than as a role.
entries.definitionCN: 指律师的实务与手艺，看作工作而非角色。

entries.definition: One who saws wood, from saw plus the same agent ending; the shape matches but the base is a tool, not law.
entries.definitionCN: 锯木的人，由 saw 加同一个施事后缀构成；外形相似，基础词却是工具而非法律。

entries.definition: A law-enforcement officer, built from law plus man; it names an officer, not a legal adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 执法官员，由 law 加 man 构成；它指警官，不是法律顾问。

entries.definition: The formal American word for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: A legal adviser or the advocates in a case, often a mass noun with a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 法律顾问或案中的辩护人，常作不可数名词，语气正式。

entries.definition: In Britain, the lawyer who advises and prepares documents rather than pleading in higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指提供咨询、准备文书而不在高等法院辩论的律师。

entries.definition: In Britain, a lawyer specially qualified to plead in the higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指有资格在高等法院出庭辩论的律师。

entries.definition: A person who pleads for another, in law or in a cause; the word stresses speaking for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人或某项事业辩护的人；这个词强调替人发声。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Norse source of law and the real agent ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 law 真实的诺斯语来源，以及真实的施事后缀。

normal.en: Law is 'what is laid down', and a lawyer is the person who works with what is laid down.
normal.cn: law 是「被放下的东西」，lawyer 就是与这些既定规则打交道的人。

normal.en: The -yer ending is a spelling of the agent ending that also built sawyer, a woodcutter.
normal.cn: -yer 是施事后缀的一种拼法，它也构成了 sawyer，即锯木人。

normal.en: Sawyer looks like lawyer but starts from a tool, so the two words share an ending and nothing else.
normal.cn: sawyer 形似 lawyer，却从工具起头，两词只共享词尾，别无其他。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the settings: a practising lawyer, a defence lawyer, a company lawyer.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：执业律师、辩护律师、公司法务。

normal.en: The plain word sits between attorney and counsel: less formal than one, less courtroom-bound than the other.
normal.cn: 这个通称夹在 attorney 与 counsel 之间：比前者随意，比后者少些法庭气。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of folders with coloured tabs, one tab for each field of law.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗，每个法律领域一个标签。

abstract.en: Picture a person reading a contract with a red pen, circling what could cost money.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人拿着红笔读合同，圈出可能花钱的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a trade that exists because rules are written down and someone must read them closely.
abstract.cn: 想象一门行业的存在理由：规则被写下来，总得有人仔细去读。

examples.en: A good lawyer tells you what not to sign, not only what to sign.
examples.cn: 好律师会告诉你什么别签，而不只是什么该签。

examples.en: The company keeps two lawyers in house and hires outside counsel for big cases.
examples.cn: 公司内部留了两名律师，大案子再请外部顾问。

examples.en: He joked that every family needs a doctor, a lawyer and a locksmith.
examples.cn: 他开玩笑说，每个家庭都需要一个医生、一个律师和一个锁匠。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the profession as a whole, through office advice, courtroom advocacy, the trade seen as a group, specialist practice and document drafting, to the sea lawyer and the mere quibbler.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整个职业开始，经办公室咨询、出庭辩护、作为群体的律师界、专长执业与文书起草，最后到「好抬杠的水手」和只会钻字眼的争辩者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of tabbed files on a desk, one clause circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公桌上一摞贴标签的卷宗，其中一条被红笔圈出。

branches.en: THE TRADE: the agent ending turns the rules into a person whose work they are.
branches.cn: 职业：施事后缀把「规则」变成以此为业的人。

branches.en: THE DESK: most of the work is reading, warning and drafting outside court.
branches.cn: 办公桌：多数工作是在法庭之外阅读、提醒与起草。

branches.en: THE VOICE AND THE BODY: the same noun covers the speaker in court and the profession as a collective force.
branches.cn: 声音与群体：同一个名词既指庭上发言者，也指作为一股力量的整个行业。

branches.en: THE NARROWING: fields and paperwork split the general word into specialisms and quiet desk work.
branches.cn: 细分：领域与文书把这个通称分成专业分工与安静的案头工作。

branches.en: THE INSULT: the trade's prestige also produces mock titles for quibblers and technical arguers.
branches.cn: 讥称：这个行业的声望也造出了挖苦人的称号，指爱抬杠与钻字眼的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is a home-built English compound: a Norse-derived noun plus a French-derived agent ending.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语本土拼装的复合词：一个源自诺斯语的名词，加一个源自法语的施事后缀。

latinIntro.en: The ending is Latin -arius, which reached English through Old French -ier; the noun law itself is not Latin but Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾是拉丁 -arius，经古法语 -ier 进入英语；而名词 law 本身并非拉丁语，而是诺斯语。

senses.title: To put something down flat or in place
senses.definition: to place something down carefully, especially so that it lies flat on a surface
senses.definitionCN: 小心地把某物放下，尤指使其平贴在表面上
senses.example: He laid the map flat on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 他把地图平铺在书桌上。
senses.why: The Old English verb was the causative partner of to lie: it meant to make something lie down, which is exactly the picture of placing an object flat.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词是「躺」的使役对应词，意为「使某物躺下」，正是一幅把东西平放下去的画面。

senses.title: To produce eggs
senses.definition: to produce an egg from the body, used of birds, fish, reptiles and insects
senses.definitionCN: 从体内产出卵，用于鸟、鱼、爬行动物和昆虫
senses.example: The hen lays an egg almost every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这只母鸡几乎每天早上下一枚蛋。
senses.why: An egg is deposited on a surface the way an object is laid down, so the same verb covers both the careful placing and the dropping of an egg.
senses.whyCN: 蛋被安置在某个表面上，就像物件被放下，于是同一个动词既指小心摆放，也指把蛋产下。

senses.title: To prepare and set a table
senses.definition: to arrange plates, knives and other items in their places for a meal
senses.definitionCN: 把盘碟、刀叉等按位置摆好，准备用餐
senses.example: She laid the table before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到来之前她把餐桌摆好了。
senses.why: Setting a table is a series of small placements, each item laid in its own place, so the general sense of placing turns into the household ritual.
senses.whyCN: 摆餐桌是一连串小小的放置动作，每件东西都被放在自己的位置上，于是泛泛的「放置」义变成了家庭里的固定仪式。

senses.title: To present or put forward a claim
senses.definition: to put forward a claim, a charge or a responsibility for others to consider
senses.definitionCN: 提出主张、指控或责任，供他人考虑
senses.example: The workers laid their demands before the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们把他们的要求摆到了经理面前。
senses.why: A claim is placed before someone as a document is placed on a table, so the physical act of laying supplies the metaphor for formal demands.
senses.whyCN: 主张被摆到某人面前，就像文件被放到桌上，于是「放置」这一物理动作提供了正式诉求的比喻。

intro.en: Lay is the Old English causative of lie: to lay something is to make it lie, and the two verbs have been confusing writers ever since.
intro.cn: lay 是古英语中 lie 的使役形式：把某物 lay 就是使它 lie，这两个动词从此一直让写作者犯难。

items.en: Lecgan meant to cause something to lie down, the causative partner of licgan, to lie.
items.cn: lecgan 意为使某物躺下，是 licgan（躺）的使役对应词。

items.en: Licgan was the intransitive verb to lie; the pair survives as lay and lie, which still confuse writers.
items.cn: licgan 是不及物动词「躺」；这一对至今保存为 lay 与 lie，仍让写作者混淆。

items.en: Middle English leyen kept the idea of placing something down, and the past tense ledde later became laid.
items.cn: 中古英语 leyen 保留「把东西放下」的意思，过去式 ledde 后来变为 laid。

items.en: Lay widened into set phrases such as lay the table, lay a trap and lay a claim, all built on placing something in position.
items.cn: lay 扩展到 lay the table、lay a trap、lay a claim 等固定说法，都建立在「把东西放到位」。

items.en: Modern English keeps laid as the past of lay, and the egg sense survives in farming and everyday speech.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 laid 为 lay 的过去式，产卵义在农业与日常口语中都还在用。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and derivatives of lay; the near-meaning group collects verbs for placing, including the pair that is most often confused with it.
note.cn: 形近组收 lay 的各种形式与派生词；近义组收表示放置的动词，包括最常与它混淆的那个词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of lay, not of lie.
entries.definitionCN: lay 的过去式与过去分词，而不是 lie 的。

entries.definition: The present participle of lay.
entries.definitionCN: lay 的现在分词。

entries.definition: A single thickness of material lying over another.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在另一层之上的一层材料。

entries.definition: To put something in a particular position.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在特定位置。

entries.definition: To move something into a position, the most general verb of placing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移到某个位置，最泛用的放置动词。

entries.definition: To put something in place carefully, often for a purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为某个目的小心地把某物放好。

entries.definition: To rest flat on a surface, the intransitive partner of lay.
entries.definitionCN: 平躺在表面上，是 lay 的不及物对应词。

normalIntro.en: The word is the active partner of lie, and its short forms hide an irregular past that catches almost every learner.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 lie 的主动对应词，它简短的形式里藏着一个几乎能难住每个学习者的不规则过去式。

normal.en: Lay is to lie as raise is to rise: lay needs an object, because something else is being made to lie.
normal.cn: lay 与 lie 的关系就像 raise 与 rise：lay 需要宾语，因为是别的东西被弄得躺下。

normal.en: The past tense is laid, never layed, which is the spelling mistake to watch for.
normal.cn: 过去式是 laid，绝不是 layed，这是最要提防的拼写错误。

normal.en: Lay the table is a fixed phrase, so the placing sense became a household routine.
normal.cn: lay the table 是固定说法，于是「放置」义成了家庭日常。

normal.en: A hen lays an egg because the egg is deposited, which is the same downward placement.
normal.cn: 母鸡 lay an egg，因为蛋被安置下来，仍是同一种向下的放置。

normal.en: Layout and layer both build on lay: an arrangement and a thickness placed over something.
normal.cn: layout 与 layer 都由 lay 构成：一个是排布，一个是铺在上面的厚度。

abstract.en: One verb covers plates, eggs and claims because all three are put down where someone will find them.
abstract.cn: 一个动词涵盖盘子、蛋和主张，因为三者都被放在别人能找到的地方。

abstract.en: The difference between lay and lie is the difference between doing something to a thing and doing something to yourself.
abstract.cn: lay 与 lie 的差别，就是对别的东西做一件事，还是对自己做一件事。

abstract.en: Every table laid before a meal is a small act of arranging the future.
abstract.cn: 每张餐前摆好的桌子，都是一次安排未来的小小动作。

examples.cn: 客人到来之前她把餐桌摆好了。

examples.en: He laid the map flat on the desk.
examples.cn: 他把地图平铺在书桌上。

examples.en: The hen lays an egg almost every morning.
examples.cn: 这只母鸡几乎每天早上下一枚蛋。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累」——东西放多了人也累；谐音记住 lay 是放置，过去式是 laid。

root: 古英语 lecgan（使躺下），是 licgan（躺）的使役动词；过去式 ledde 后演变为 laid。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is causing something to lie in place; it branches into setting a table, depositing an egg, and laying a claim before someone.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是使某物躺放在位；由此分出摆餐具、产卵，以及把主张摆到某人面前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands smoothing a cloth flat across a tabletop.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把一块布在桌面上抹平。

branches.en: a map smoothed flat on a desk
branches.cn: 在桌上被抹平的地图

branches.en: forks and plates set in their places
branches.cn: 刀叉与盘子各就各位

branches.en: a hen stepping away from a warm egg
branches.cn: 母鸡离开一枚温热的蛋

branches.en: a trap hidden under dry leaves
branches.cn: 藏在干叶下的陷阱

branches.en: demands placed before a manager
branches.cn: 摆到经理面前的要求

intro.en: The word is a bare Old English verb with an irregular past; modern English builds its family with -er and with compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词是光秃秃的古英语动词，过去式不规则；现代英语用 -er 与复合方式扩展它的词族。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for lay; it and its partner lie are Germanic verbs.
latinIntro.cn: lay 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它与对应的 lie 都是日耳曼语动词。

definition_zh: 层；层次；地层；涂层；产蛋鸡
definition_en: a thickness or sheet of material covering a surface; one of several levels in a system; a hen that lays eggs
core_image: 一张一张薄片叠起来，像千层饼的横截面，每一层都清晰可数
scene: 地质课上，老师用铲子切开岩壁，露出水平排列的一层层岩石。他指着说：Each layer was laid down in a different age.
sceneCN: 这里 layer 是「岩层、地层」（第 3 个义项：地质沉积层）；句意：每一层岩石都是在不同年代沉积下来的。图中可辨识物件：岩壁、铲子、水平岩层、地质锤。

derivatives.zh: 分层的；有层次的
分层；层叠；压条繁殖
多层的；多层结构
夹层；中间层

senses.title: A sheet laid over a surface
senses.titleCN: 铺在表面上的一层：涂层、薄层
senses.definition: a thickness or sheet of material that covers a surface
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一层材料或一片物质
senses.example: A thin layer of dust covered the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上覆盖着一层薄薄的灰。
senses.why: Layer is lay + -er: 'that which is laid'. A layer is material placed down on a surface, seen as one sheet rather than as a mass.
senses.whyCN: layer 是 lay 加 -er，即“被铺下的东西”。一层就是把材料铺在表面上，被看作一片，而不是一团。

senses.title: One level in a stack of levels
senses.titleCN: 层层结构中的一级：层次
senses.definition: one of several levels in a system, idea or organization, each built on or above another
senses.definitionCN: 系统、思想或组织中的若干层级之一，每一层建立在另一层之上
senses.example: The novel works on several layers of meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在好几层意义上成立。
senses.why: Anything that can be laid down one piece over another can be imagined as a stack. Ideas and organizations borrow the physical stack and call each level a layer.
senses.whyCN: 任何能一层压一层铺放的东西，都可以被想象成一摞。思想与组织借用这个物理堆叠，把每一级称为一层。

senses.title: A stratum in the earth
senses.definition: in geology, a band of rock or soil of one kind, deposited at a particular period
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中，某一时期沉积形成的同一种岩石或土壤带
senses.example: The fossils were found in a layer of limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 化石是在一层石灰岩中发现的。
senses.why: Sediment settles in sheets, one age on top of another. Geology sees the earth's history as a stack of layers, so the word becomes a technical term for a stratum.
senses.whyCN: 沉积物一片一片落下，一个年代压在另一个年代上。地质学把地球历史看成一摞层，于是这个词成为“地层”的术语。

senses.title: A band around the planet
senses.titleCN: 包围地球的一带：大气层
senses.definition: in geography, a distinct band of the atmosphere or ocean at a particular height or depth
senses.definitionCN: 地理学中，大气或海洋在特定高度或深度上的一条明显带
senses.example: The ozone layer protects us from harmful radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 臭氧层保护我们免受有害辐射。
senses.why: The atmosphere is arranged in shells, one above another. Each shell is a layer because it can be drawn as a band laid over the one below.
senses.whyCN: 大气按壳层排列，一层在另一层之上。每个壳层都是一层，因为它可以被画成覆盖在下面那层上的一条带。

senses.title: A level in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的一层：分层架构
senses.definition: in computing, one level of a system or protocol that communicates with the levels above and below it
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中，与上下层通信的系统或协议的一级
senses.example: The application layer sits above the network layer.
senses.exampleCN: 应用层位于网络层之上。
senses.why: Software designers picture a system as a stack of levels, each hiding the details of the one below. The physical stack of sheets becomes an architecture.
senses.whyCN: 软件设计者把系统想象成一摞层级，每一层隐藏下面一层的细节。物理的薄片堆叠变成了架构。

senses.title: One coat of paint
senses.definition: one application or coat of paint, varnish or another covering material
senses.definitionCN: 油漆、清漆或其他覆盖材料的一次涂布
senses.example: The wall needs two more layers of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙还需要再刷两层漆。
senses.why: Painting is the most literal act of laying down a sheet of material. Each pass adds one more layer, and the old surface disappears under it.
senses.whyCN: 刷漆是最字面的“铺下一层材料”。每刷一遍就多一层，旧表面被盖在下面。

senses.title: Clothing stacked for warmth
senses.titleCN: 为保暖叠穿：一层层衣物
senses.definition: one garment or set of garments worn over another, especially for warmth
senses.definitionCN: 穿在另一件外面的一件或多件衣物，尤为了保暖
senses.example: Wear several thin layers instead of one thick coat.
senses.exampleCN: 穿几层薄衣服，而不是一件厚外套。
senses.why: Dressing in layers is stacking sheets of fabric around the body. Each garment is a layer, and warmth comes from the trapped air between them.
senses.whyCN: 分层穿衣就是把一片片布料叠在身体周围。每件衣服是一层，温暖来自层与层之间被困住的空气。

senses.title: The hen that lays
senses.definition: a hen kept for laying eggs, or a hen that lays eggs regularly
senses.definitionCN: 为产蛋而饲养的母鸡，或定期下蛋的母鸡
senses.example: The farm keeps two hundred layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养了两百只产蛋鸡。
senses.why: This is the agent sense of -er: a layer is 'one who lays'. It is not a sheet at all, but the same suffix that names the one performing the action.
senses.whyCN: 这是 -er 的施动者义：layer 就是“下蛋的那一个”。它完全不是薄片，而是同一个后缀用来命名执行动作的主体。

senses.title: Layering a plant
senses.titleCN: 压条繁殖：layer 的园艺动词
senses.definition: in gardening, to make a stem root while still attached to the parent plant, or the resulting rooted branch
senses.definitionCN: 园艺中使枝条在仍连着母株时生根，或指这样生根的枝条
senses.example: They layered the rose bush to produce a new plant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这株玫瑰进行压条，以培育新植株。
senses.why: The gardener bends a stem down and 'lays' it under soil. The new plant is produced by a laying-down, so the method and the verb share the original physical action.
senses.whyCN: 园丁把枝条弯下并“铺”在土里。新植株由一次“铺下”产生，所以这种方法与动词共享最初的物理动作。

intro.en: Layer is an English agent noun: lay + -er, 'one who or that which lays'. Lay goes back to Old English lecgan 'to place', from the causative of the verb that became lie. The 'sheet of material' sense developed later, probably under some influence from French cookery terms.
intro.cn: layer 是英语的施动名词：lay 加 -er，即“放置的人或物”。lay 可追溯到古英语 lecgan“放置”，它是后来变成 lie 的动词的使役形式。“一层材料”的义项发展较晚，可能受到法语烹饪用语的一些影响。

items.en: The root *legh- meant 'to lie down, lay'. It underlies English lie, lay and law (something 'laid down'), and German liegen and legen.
items.cn: 词根 *legh- 意为“躺下、放下”。它是英语 lie、lay 和 law（“被放下的东西”）以及德语 liegen、legen 的深层来源。

items.en: Lecgan meant 'to place on the ground or another surface; place in order; put down'. It was the causative of licgan 'to lie': to lay is to cause to lie.
items.cn: lecgan 意为“放在地上或其他表面上；按顺序摆放；放下”。它是 licgan“躺”的使役形式：lay 就是“使……躺下”。

items.en: Layer is first recorded in the late 14th century as 'one who or that lays', especially a mason who lays stones. This is the agent-noun sense of -er.
items.cn: layer 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“放置的人或物”，尤指砌石的泥瓦匠。这是 -er 的施动名词义。

items.en: The passive sense 'a thickness of material laid over a surface' is recorded by the 1610s. Because the earliest English uses were in cookery, the sense may have been influenced by French liue 'binding', a word used of a thickened sauce.
items.cn: 被动义“铺在表面上的一层材料”记录于 17 世纪 10 年代。由于英语最早的用法出现在烹饪中，这个义项可能受到法语 liue“黏合”的影响，后者用于浓稠酱汁。

items.en: The hen sense 'a hen that lays eggs' is recorded by 1707. Layer cake is attested from 1875, naming a cake made of stacked layers.
items.cn: “下蛋的母鸡”义项记录于 1707 年。layer cake（千层蛋糕）记录于 1875 年，指由叠层制成的蛋糕。

items.en: The verb layer is from 1779 in horticulture, as a method of plant propagation. The general sense 'form into layers' is attested by 1852.
items.cn: 动词 layer 来自 1779 年的园艺用法，指一种植物繁殖方法。“形成层”的一般义项记录于 1852 年。

note.en: The look-alike group is the lay/layer family; the near-meaning group contains words for sheets and levels, each from a different material or scale.
note.cn: 形近组是 lay/layer 词族；近义组是薄片与层级类词，各自的材料或尺度不同。

entries.definition: to put something down on a surface; to place in order. It is the verb behind layer, and its past tense is laid, not layed.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在表面上；按顺序摆放。它是 layer 背后的动词，过去式是 laid，不是 layed。

entries.definition: the act of putting something down, or of a hen producing an egg. It is the -ing form of lay.
entries.definitionCN: 放下某物的动作，或母鸡下蛋。它是 lay 的 -ing 形式。

entries.definition: arranged in layers, or having several levels. The past participle became an adjective describing a stacked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 分层排列的，或具有多个层次的。过去分词变成形容词，描述堆叠结构。

entries.definition: a layer of rock or soil, especially one of many deposited in sequence. It is the technical Latin word for a geological layer.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或土壤的一层，尤指按顺序沉积的许多层之一。它是地质层的拉丁技术词。

entries.definition: a thin layer of a substance covering a surface. It stresses the material spread over something, often for protection.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一薄层物质。它强调铺在表面的材料，常带保护目的。

entries.definition: a very thin layer or membrane. It is thinner than a typical layer and often continuous and transparent.
entries.definitionCN: 极薄的一层或膜。它比一般的 layer 更薄，常是连续而透明的。

entries.definition: one of several levels in a hierarchy, especially when they are ranked. It is the social or organizational counterpart of a physical layer.
entries.definitionCN: 等级体系中的一层，尤指被排序的层级。它是物理 layer 在社会或组织中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: lay 'place down' + -er, plus the ordinary family layered, layering, multilayer, interlayer. The 'sheet' sense came later than the 'one who lays' sense.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构件：lay“放下”加 -er，以及常用词族 layered、layering、multilayer、interlayer。“薄层”义晚于“放置者”义出现。

normal.en: Layer = lay + -er. The first meaning was 'one who lays', like a mason laying stones; only later did it mean 'that which is laid' as a sheet.
normal.cn: layer = lay + -er。最早的意思是“放置者”，像砌石的泥瓦匠；后来才表示“被铺下的东西”，即一层。

normal.en: A hen that lays eggs is also a layer, because -er can name the doer. The same suffix gives both the mason and the sheet.
normal.cn: 下蛋的母鸡也是 layer，因为 -er 可以命名动作的执行者。同一个后缀既给出泥瓦匠，也给出薄层。

normal.en: A geological layer is history stacked: each sheet of sediment is an older page under a newer one.
normal.cn: 地层就是被叠起来的历史：每一片沉积物都是压在更新一页下面的旧页。

normal.en: In computing, a layer hides the layer below it. The stack is physical in origin and architectural in use.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，一层隐藏下面一层。这个堆叠起源于物理，却被用于架构。

normal.en: Fixed patterns: a thin layer of, the ozone layer, layers of meaning, and in layers.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：a thin layer of（薄薄一层）、the ozone layer（臭氧层）、layers of meaning（层层含义）、in layers（分层地）。

abstract.en: A layer is both a cover and a record: it hides what is below while preserving it.
abstract.cn: 一层既是覆盖，也是记录：它遮住下面的东西，同时把它保存下来。

abstract.en: Complexity is often just depth: when a thing has too many layers, we stop seeing the surface and start seeing a system.
abstract.cn: 复杂往往只是深度：当一个东西层数太多，我们就不再看到表面，而开始看到一个系统。

abstract.en: Every layer was laid by someone or something. The word keeps the action inside the noun, which is why a stratum can be read as a date.
abstract.cn: 每一层都是由某个力量铺下的。这个词把动作保留在名词里，所以一层地层可以被读成一个年代。

examples.en: A thick layer of snow covered the car.
examples.cn: 厚厚的一层雪盖住了汽车。

examples.en: The problem has several layers that must be solved separately.
examples.cn: 这个问题有几层，必须分别解决。

examples.en: The farmer keeps a hundred layers for eggs.
examples.cn: 农场主养了一百只产蛋鸡。

dict_mnemonic.text: “累·尔”——累（了就把）尔（等薄片）一层层叠起来 → layer 层

root: 由英语动词 lay“放下、铺下”加施动后缀 -er 构成；lay 源于古英语 lecgan“放置”，再上溯到原始印欧语 *legh-“躺下、放下”，核心是“被铺下去的一片”，也保留“放置者”的施动义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of layer, all one action: something is laid down on something else. Dust, meaning, rock, atmosphere, software, paint, clothing, a laying hen and a propagated stem each come from that same verb lay.
sensesIntro.cn: layer 的九个义项都是同一个动作：某物被铺在另一物上。灰尘、意义、岩石、大气、软件、油漆、衣物、下蛋的母鸡和压条的枝条，都来自同一个动词 lay。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin sheets stacked one on another, each visible as a separate band.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张张薄片叠在一起，每一片都能被看成分明的一带。

branches.en: MATERIAL LAID ON A SURFACE: dust, paint and clothing are added as sheets over what is already there.
branches.cn: 铺在表面上的材料：灰尘、油漆和衣物都是一片片加在已有之物上面。

branches.en: LEVELS IN A SYSTEM: meanings and software are built as stacks, each level resting on another.
branches.cn: 系统中的层级：意义与软件都以堆叠方式建立，每一层依托另一层。

branches.en: NATURAL BANDS: rock strata record ages, and atmospheric shells wrap the planet in bands.
branches.cn: 自然界的层带：岩层记录年代，大气壳层以带状包裹地球。

branches.en: THE DOER: a laying hen is a layer because -er can name the one performing the action.
branches.cn: 执行者：下蛋的母鸡是 layer，因为 -er 可以命名执行动作的主体。

branches.en: THE HORTICULTURAL ACT: a stem is laid under soil so that it roots, turning the verb back into a physical laying-down.
branches.cn: 园艺动作：枝条被铺在土下以便生根，使动词回到物理上的“铺下”。

intro.en: Layer is an English compound of lay + -er. Its family is built with -ed, -ing, and the prefixes multi- and inter-.
intro.cn: layer 是 lay + -er 的英语复合词。它的词族用 -ed、-ing，以及前缀 multi-、inter- 构成。

latinIntro.en: Layer has no Latin root; it is native English. The Latin word for a geological layer is stratum, from sternere 'to spread out', which is a useful contrast rather than a source.
latinIntro.cn: layer 没有拉丁词根，是本族英语词。地质层的拉丁词是 stratum，来自 sternere“铺开”，这是有用的对照，而不是来源。

items.meaning: a sheet laid over a surface; one who lays
items.meaningCN: 层；放置者（-er 表施动者或事物）
items.example: A layer of ice formed on the pond.

items.meaning: several sheets or levels; the act of layering
items.meaningCN: 多层；分层（复数或第三人称单数）

items.example: The story has a layered structure.

items.meaning: the act of arranging in layers; plant propagation
items.example: Layering is a simple way to propagate plants.
items.exampleCN: 压条是一种简单的植物繁殖方法。
这种薄膜使用多层包装。

items.meaningCN: 夹层；中间层（inter- 表之间）
items.example: A thin interlayer separates the two sheets.
items.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的夹层把两片材料隔开。

items.meaning: a cake made of stacked layers
items.example: She baked a chocolate layer cake.
items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个巧克力千层蛋糕。

items.meaning: the atmospheric band rich in ozone
items.example: The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet light.

items.meaningCN: 放置；铺下（layer 的基础动词）
items.example: She laid the cloth on the table.

latinEntries.meaning: a layer, bed, pavement (not the source of layer)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 层；地层（并非 layer 的来源，仅作对照）

latinEntries.meaning: bed, couch (same PIE root as lay)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 床；卧榻（与 lay 同出一个原始印欧语词根）

definition_zh: 懒惰的；慵懒的；懒洋洋的；马虎的
definition_en: unwilling to work or make effort, pleasantly relaxed, slow and without force, or done without care
core_image: 午后斜阳照进院子，一个人摊在躺椅上，手边的杯子够不着也不愿起身
scene: 午后的院子里，躺椅上的人伸手够了够杯子，又把手放下。It was a lazy afternoon, and nobody wanted to move.
sceneCN: 这里是「慵懒的、悠闲的」（第 2 个义项：轻松惬意、不费力的状态）；句意为那是一个慵懒的午后，没人愿意动。可辨识画面：斜阳、躺椅、手边的杯子。

pos.zh: 懒惰的；慵懒的；懒洋洋的；马虎的

derivatives.zh: 由 lazy 变 y 为 i 再加 -ly 构成，义为「懒洋洋地」
由 lazy 变 y 为 i 再加 -ness 构成，义为「懒惰」
由 lazy 与 bones 复合，义为「懒骨头」
一般认为由 lazy 逆构而成，义为「懒散地打发时间」

senses.title: Unwilling to work or make effort
senses.definition: not willing to work or to make any effort
senses.definitionCN: 不愿意工作或付出任何努力
senses.example: He is too lazy to wash his own cup.
senses.exampleCN: 他懒得连自己的杯子都不洗。
senses.why: The word probably came from a Low German term for weak or useless, so laziness began as a body that would not serve.
senses.whyCN: 这个词很可能来自低地德语中表示虚弱、无用的说法，所以懒惰最初是身体不肯出力。

senses.title: Pleasantly relaxed
senses.definition: relaxed and slow in a pleasant way, as of a warm afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 轻松而缓慢，令人愉快，如温暖的午后
senses.example: We spent a lazy afternoon by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边度过了一个慵懒的午后。
senses.why: If a body refuses effort, the same word can describe a time when no effort is asked for, and the refusal turns into comfort.
senses.whyCN: 身体若不肯出力，同一个词也能形容一段不需要出力的时间，拒绝就变成了惬意。

senses.title: Slow and without force
senses.titleCN: 懒洋洋的；缓慢不用力的
senses.definition: moving or flowing slowly, without energy
senses.definitionCN: 动作或流动缓慢，不带力气
senses.example: A lazy smile spread across his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上浮起懒洋洋的笑。
senses.why: The idea of withheld effort moves easily onto movements and sounds, so slow and soft things are called lazy too.
senses.whyCN: 「不肯出力」的想法很容易挪到动作与声音上，于是缓慢柔和的东西也被说成 lazy。

senses.title: Careless, done without proper effort
senses.definition: done without care or attention, as a lazy attempt
senses.definitionCN: 做事不细心、不用心，如敷衍的尝试
senses.example: The report was a lazy piece of work.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告写得很敷衍。
senses.why: When effort is withheld from work that needs it, the word stops being pleasant and becomes a criticism of quality.
senses.whyCN: 当该出力的活被省了力气，这个词就不再惬意，而成了对质量的批评。

intro.en: This word has no known Old English form; it appears in the sixteenth century, probably from a Low German or Dutch term for weakness.
intro.cn: 这个词没有已知的古英语形态，十六世纪才出现，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱说法。

items.en: No Old English form is known, so the path before the sixteenth century is uncertain.
items.cn: 没有已知的古英语形式，十六世纪之前的来路并不确定。

items.en: The word is first recorded in the sixteenth century, probably from a Low German or Dutch term for weak or useless.
items.cn: 这个词最早见于十六世纪，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱、无用的说法。

items.en: English lazy appears first meaning disinclined to work, with the bodily sense of weakness still near.
items.cn: 英语 lazy 最初表示不愿干活，身体虚弱的意味还很近。

items.en: The pleasant sense of a relaxed time grows later, especially in phrases like a lazy afternoon.
items.cn: 「悠闲时光」的愉快义出现较晚，尤见于 a lazy afternoon 这类说法。

items.en: Modern English uses lazy for people, for comfortable slow time, and for work done without care.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lazy 形容人、形容舒适缓慢的时间，也形容不用心做出的活。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on the same stem or a similar shape; the near-meaning group collects other words for idleness and slowness.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一词干构成的或形状相近的形式；近义组收其他表示懒散与迟缓的词。

entries.definition: To spend time doing very little, formed from lazy.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎什么也不做地打发时间，由 lazy 逆构而来。

entries.definition: In a slow, relaxed manner.
entries.definitionCN: 以缓慢放松的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being unwilling to work.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿工作的性质。

entries.definition: Slightly misty, not clear to see.
entries.definitionCN: 略有雾、看不清楚；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Not working or not in use.
entries.definitionCN: 不工作或不使用的。

entries.definition: Disliking effort or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 厌恶出力或活动的。

entries.definition: Moving or reacting more slowly than usual.
entries.definitionCN: 移动或反应比平常慢的。

entries.definition: Without energy or enthusiasm.
entries.definitionCN: 没有精力或热情的。

normalIntro.en: With no native Old English shape, the word is held together by an uncertain foreign source and the English endings that grew on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词没有土生的古英语形态，靠一个不确定的外来来源与长在它上面的英语词尾支撑起来。

normal.en: Lazy has no known Old English form; it appears in the sixteenth century, probably from Low German or Dutch.
normal.cn: lazy 没有已知的古英语形式，十六世纪才出现，一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语。

normal.en: Laze is a back-formation: the shorter verb was cut from the longer adjective.
normal.cn: laze 是逆构词：较短的动词是从较长的形容词上切下来的。

normal.en: Lazily and laziness change y to i before the suffix, as happy becomes happily.
normal.cn: lazily 与 laziness 在加后缀前把 y 变 i，就像 happy 变 happily。

normal.en: Lazybones is lazy plus bones, a joking name for a person who will not move.
normal.cn: lazybones 是 lazy 加 bones，是给不肯动的人起的玩笑称呼。

normal.en: A lazy afternoon is pleasant, but a lazy attempt is a criticism of the work.
normal.cn: a lazy afternoon 是惬意的，而 a lazy attempt 是对工作的批评。

abstract.en: The word began as a body that would not serve and ended as a description of comfort, a shift in who is judging.
abstract.cn: 这个词从「不肯出力的身体」走到「舒适的描述」，变的是谁在评判。

abstract.en: Calling a person lazy is a moral judgement, while calling an afternoon lazy is a gift of permission.
abstract.cn: 说一个人 lazy 是道德评判，而说一个午后 lazy 是允许人放松。

abstract.en: English separates the refusal of work from the need for rest by tone rather than by word.
abstract.cn: 英语用语气而不是用词，把「拒绝干活」与「需要休息」区分开。

examples.en: He is too lazy to wash his own cup.
examples.cn: 他懒得连自己的杯子都不洗。

examples.en: We spent a lazy afternoon by the river.
examples.cn: 我们在河边度过了一个慵懒的午后。

examples.en: The report was a lazy piece of work.
examples.cn: 那份报告写得很敷衍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累极」——懒到把累极的身体摊在椅子上，什么也不想做；记住 lazy 是懒惰的。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为来自低地德语或荷兰语中表示虚弱、无用的说法，十六世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a body withholding effort; the senses then add pleasant slowness, slow movement, and work done without care.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一具不肯出力的身体；义项由此加上惬意的缓慢、动作的迟缓，以及不用心做出的活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for a cup and giving up halfway.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向杯子，伸到一半又放下。

branches.en: a cup left unwashed beside a chair
branches.cn: 椅子旁没洗的杯子

branches.en: a long warm afternoon with nobody moving
branches.cn: 漫长温暖、无人起身的午后

branches.en: a slow smile spreading without hurry
branches.cn: 不急不忙地铺开的笑

branches.en: a report finished in ten careless minutes
branches.cn: 十分钟草草写完的报告

branches.en: a body sunk deep into a deck chair
branches.cn: 深陷在躺椅里的身体

definition_zh: 领导；带领；导致；领先
definition_en: to guide or be in charge of others, to cause something to happen, or to be ahead
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，身后的人跟着他选的方向
scene: 队伍在岔路口停下，向导抬手示意大家往左边走。She led the group through the narrow pass.
sceneCN: 这里是「带领、引导」（第 1 个义项：动词，指走在前头带路）；句意为她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。图中可辨识物件：岔路口、向导的手势、狭窄山口。

derivatives.zh: 由 lead 加 -er 构成，义为「领导者；领袖」
由 lead 加 -ing 构成，义为「领先的；主要的」
由 leader 加 -ship 构成，义为「领导；领导力」
由 mis-（错误地）加 lead 构成，义为「误导」

senses.title: To guide someone along a way
senses.definition: to go in front of others and show them the way
senses.definitionCN: 走在别人前面并为他们指路
senses.example: She led the group through the narrow pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to cause someone to go; the leader is the one who sets the direction of that going.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「使某人走」，带路的人就是决定「往哪走」的那个人。

senses.title: To be in charge of people or an activity
senses.definition: to direct a group, organization or activity and be responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 指挥一个群体、组织或活动并对其负责
senses.example: He leads a team of twelve engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 他领导着一支十二名工程师的团队。
senses.why: From physically going first it is a short step to deciding for others, so lead comes to mean holding authority.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上走在最前，很容易走到「替别人做决定」，于是 lead 转而指掌握权力。

senses.title: To cause something to happen
senses.definition: to be the cause or route by which a result happens
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个结果发生的原因或路径
senses.example: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足可能导致严重的健康问题。
senses.why: A path leads to a place; events also have paths, so lead to names the route by which one thing brings about another.
senses.whyCN: 一条路通向一个地方；事情也有路径，所以 lead to 指一件事带出另一件事的路线。

senses.title: To be ahead in a race or competition
senses.definition: to have more points or be further forward than others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中比别人得分多或位置更靠前
senses.example: Our team leads by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队领先两球。
senses.why: The one in front is literally leading the line, and the racing sense keeps that simple picture of position.
senses.whyCN: 走在最前的人字面上就在「带」着队伍，竞赛义保留了这个简单的方位画面。

senses.title: The position of being ahead
senses.definition: the first place or advantage held over others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争中占据的第一名次或优势
senses.example: The champion held the lead until the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军一直保持领先直到最后一圈。
senses.why: The verb's sense of being in front turns into a noun naming that front position.
senses.whyCN: 动词「处在前面」的意思转成一个名词，指那个靠前的位置。

senses.title: A clue in an investigation
senses.definition: a piece of information that suggests where to look next
senses.definitionCN: 提示下一步该往哪里查的信息
senses.example: The police followed a new lead.
senses.exampleCN: 警方追查了一条新线索。
senses.why: A lead is something that leads you somewhere; in an investigation it is the information that pulls the search forward.
senses.whyCN: lead 是能把你带到某处的东西；在调查里，它就是推动搜查往前走的信息。

intro.en: Lead comes from an Old English verb meaning to cause to go, and it has kept the picture of someone walking in front.
intro.cn: lead 来自古英语中意为「使……走」的动词，一直保留着「有人走在前面」的画面。

items.en: Lædan meant to cause someone to go, to guide or to bring along a way.
items.cn: lædan 意为使某人走、引导或沿路带领。

items.en: The reconstructed verb *laidijan is related to the noun for a path or way.
items.cn: 重构动词 *laidijan 与表示「道路、路径」的名词有关。

items.en: Middle English leden keeps the sense of guiding and adds the idea of being first in a group.
items.cn: 中古英语 leden 保留引导义，并添上「在群体中最先」的意思。

items.en: The noun lead, meaning the first place, appears in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 表示第一名的名词 lead 在十五世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English adds lead to 'cause' and lead as a clue, while the metal lead is a different word with a different vowel.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 lead to（导致）与「线索」义；金属铅则是另一个词，元音也不同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflections and relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for guiding and being first.
note.cn: 形近组收动词的变形与同族词；近义组收表示引导与领先的词。

entries.definition: To organize and carry out an activity.

normalIntro.en: The past tense led drops the a of the present, and the family shows how guiding, leading and causing are one motion.
normalIntro.cn: 过去式 led 去掉了现在式中的 a；词族显示引导、领导与导致是同一种运动。

normal.en: The past tense is led, not leaded: lead, led, led.
normal.cn: 过去式是 led，不是 leaded：lead、led、led。

normal.en: Leader adds -er: the one who leads.
normal.cn: leader 加 -er，指带路的人。

normal.en: Lead to means to cause a result, as a road leads to a town.
normal.cn: lead to 意为导致结果，就像路通向城镇。

normal.en: Take the lead means to move into first place.
normal.cn: take the lead 意为取得领先。

normal.en: The metal lead is spelled the same but pronounced /led/ and has a different origin.
normal.cn: 金属铅拼写相同但读 /led/，词源也不同。

abstract.en: A word for walking in front turns into a word for authority because direction is a kind of decision.
abstract.cn: 一个「走在前面」的词变成「权力」的词，因为方向本身就是一种决定。

abstract.en: Lead to shows that causation is imagined as a path with a destination.
abstract.cn: lead to 说明因果关系被想象成一条有终点的路。

abstract.en: A clue is called a lead because information, too, can point a way.
abstract.cn: 线索被称为 lead，因为信息也能指出一条路。

examples.cn: 她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。

examples.en: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「走在前面」；由带路扩展到掌权、导致结果、处于领先，以及为调查指路。

core.cn: 核心意象：一个人走在最前面选方向，其余人跟着走。

definition_en: a person or thing that guides, directs or is ahead of others
core_image: 队伍最前面的人回头看了一眼，确认后面的人都还跟着，然后继续走
scene: 出发前，队伍最前面的人回头清点人数，确认没有人掉队才继续前进。The group chose a new leader before the season began.
sceneCN: 这里指「带领群体的那个人」（第 1 个义项：群体的领导者）；句意为赛季开始前，这个团体选出了一位新的领导者。可辨识物件：队伍、背包、路口、名册、手杖。
